CHAPTER 1. GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 31000. Purpose, Authority and Scope.
(a) These HDFC Regulations (Regulations) establish rules and procedures for the
administration of multifamily affordable housing programs administered by the
Housing Development and Finance Committee (HDFC).
(b) These Regulations implement and interpret AB 179 (Chapter 68, Statutes of 2026)
and Part 18 (commencing with Health & Saf. Code, § 54920), which establish
HDFC and its Executive Committee (EC) and authorize the consolidated statewide
administration of multifamily affordable housing programs.
(c) Consistent with statutory direction, administration of programs under these
Regulations requires ongoing coordination with the California Department of
Housing and Community Development (HCD), the California Housing Finance
Agency (CalHFA), the California Debt Limit Allocation Committee (CDLAC) and the
California Tax Credit Allocation Committee (CTCAC).
(d) Where these Regulations reference requirements, procedures, or submissions
associated with another agency, including but not limited to CTCAC, such
references shall be understood to incorporate those requirements as HDFC’s own.
(e) These Regulations do not use or incorporate the Uniform Multifamily Regulations
(25 CCR § 8300 et seq.) (UMRs) for HDFC-funded Projects. Any statutory or
program references to the UMRs or “successor” UMRs shall be deemed to refer to
these Regulations.
(f) These Regulations shall not apply to projects seeking solely an HDFC letter of
support for access to the HDFC Qualified Residential Rental Project (QRRP) Pool,
other than the provisions herein that govern the process and timing for obtaining
such letter.
(g) Applicability of HDFC Regulations to projects with HCD Awards received prior to
adoption of these HDFC Regulations. HDFC shall continue to collaborate with
partner agencies, including HCD, to streamline where feasible and permitted by law.
(1) Projects that have already received one or more HCD funding awards prior to
adoption of the HDFC Regulations and are not seeking additional gap financing
through HDFC shall continue to be governed by the terms of their original
award(s), and HCD will continue to process those closings. This includes
projects that received funding from the multifamily affordable housing programs
specified in Health & Saf. Code, § 54920(f). As is typical, HCD will continue to
work with past awardees to reconcile any conflicts between award terms,
including elevating issues to the HCD Director as needed.
(2) Projects that have received one or more HCD funding awards prior to adoption
of the HDFC Regulations, and that subsequently apply to and are awarded by
HDFC for additional gap financing shall be governed by HDFC Regulations, to
the extent permissible by law. Applicants with prior HCD awards shall agree, as
a condition of HDFC subsidy, that HDFC shall close existing HCD loans and that
these HDFC Regulations shall govern, to the fullest extent permissible by law
and in conformance with any applicable federal requirements. In the event that a
Sponsor is not reasonably able to comply with a requirement of the HDFC
Regulations with respect to an HCD funding award without jeopardizing or
materially delaying the loan closing, the Executive Director shall consider, on a
case-by-case basis, permitting compliance with one or more terms of the original
award to the reasonable extent necessary to resolve the issue.

§ 31005. Coordination with CDLAC and CTCAC Programs.
(a) HDFC Pool. Pursuant to Gov. Code, § 8869.84(b), beginning January 1, 2027, and
through July 1, 2029, at least 50% of the state ceiling allocated to the QRRP Pool
will be reserved for HDFC-approved Projects.
(b) Annual Demand Coordination and Reallocation. Beginning in calendar year 2028
and annually thereafter, no later than March 1, HDFC will estimate its projected
demand for QRRP Bonds for that calendar year and coordinate with CDLAC to
request additional allocation or determine the portion, if any, of its allocation
anticipated to remain unused by HDFC during that calendar year.
(c) Multifamily Pipeline Projects Requesting QRRP Bonds and 4% Tax Credits (2027
Transition Year). Until November 1, 2027, the bond issuer for Multifamily Pipeline
Projects may apply directly to CDLAC and CTCAC for an allocation from the 2027
HDFC Pool with a letter of support from HDFC. After November 1, 2027, eligible
applicants requesting bonds and/or 4% tax credits from the HDFC Pool must apply
directly to HDFC.
(d) Projects Requesting HDFC funds with QRRP Bonds and 4% Tax Credits. HDFC will
transmit applications to CDLAC and CTCAC, as appropriate in accordance with
CDLAC regulations (4 CCR § 5110), for any HDFC awarded applications that
requested bonds and/or 4% tax credits.
(e) State Low-Income Housing Tax Credits Coordination.
(1) Projects Requesting HDFC Funds with State Tax Credits. HDFC may award
funds to Projects requesting state tax low-income housing tax credits. All HDFC-
funded Projects pursuing state tax credits shall comply with applicable CTCAC
eligibility, application, and allocation requirements under CCR Title 4, Div. 17,
Chapter 1. Tax credit awards are subject to CTCAC and CDLAC award criteria,
schedules, and discretion
(2) Mixed Income Program. Pursuant to Rev. & Tax. Code, §§ 12206(g)(1)(B),
17058(g)(1)(B), and 23610.5(g)(1)(B), CTCAC annually sets aside up to $200
million to projects awarded funding from the MIP annually. HDFC as the
administrator of MIP will designate MIP subsidy awards for state tax credits
allocated for MIP by CTCAC. State tax credit awards shall comply with CTCAC
eligibility and allocation requirements consistent with existing law.
(f) Federal 9% Low-Income Housing Tax Credit Coordination.
(1) Projects Requesting HDFC Funds with Federal Low-Income Housing Tax
Credits. HDFC may transmit applications to CTCAC for any HDFC awarded
applications that requested federal 9% tax credits. All HDFC-funded Projects
pursuing federal 9% tax credits shall comply with applicable CTCAC eligibility,
application, underwriting, and allocation requirements under CCR Title 4, Div. 17,
Chapter 1.
(2) Coordination Within Existing CTCAC Priority Allocations. HDFC shall seek
coordination with CTCAC to establish predictable financing pathways for HDFC-
funded Projects to secure CTCAC tax credit awards, with particular emphasis on
Projects eligible for existing rural, special needs, and nonprofit set-asides and
other shared housing priorities recognized under CTCAC requirements. Nothing
in this section independently establishes or modifies a CTCAC allocation or
preference.
(3) Programming HDFC Resources. In selecting projects for HDFC financing, HDFC
shall seek to size its subsidy commitments to projects requesting 9% tax credits
consistent with the reasonably anticipated amount of 9% credits available for
allocation by CTCAC. To the extent CTCAC establishes dedicated credit
amounts or other predictable allocation mechanisms for HDFC-funded Projects,
HDFC shall size and schedule corresponding subsidy commitments based on the
anticipated credit capacity, demonstrated eligible demand, project-level financing
needs, and available HDFC resources.
(4) Application and Award Coordination. HDFC shall publish procedures identifying
the applicable 9% tax credit application process and aligning HDFC program
requirements, schedules, and materials with those required by CTCAC. HDFC
commitments shall be structured to satisfy applicable CTCAC requirements and
remain effective through the designated tax credit award decision, subject to
stated conditions. Tax credit awards shall remain subject to CTCAC approval
under the applicable allocation process.
(5) Unsuccessful Applications. HDFC shall establish and disclose deadlines for
Projects unsuccessful in obtaining 9% tax credits to release their HDFC
commitments for disencumbrance and inclusion in the next HDFC funding round.

§ 32012. Uses of Funds.
(a) Funds shall be used only for eligible costs directly related to the design, acquisition,
or development of the Project under this section and are subject to the applicable
program-specific statutes and requirements described in Chapter 3, which will
control in the event of any conflict. All costs must be necessary and reasonable for
the Project’s scope and geographic context, as determined by HDFC. Eligible costs
include, but are not limited to the following:
(1) Property Acquisition costs, including lease payments;
(2) Architectural, Appraisal, engineering, environmental, legal and other consulting
costs, and fees, which are directly related to the planning and execution of the
Project, and which are incurred through third-party contracts;
(3) Escrow, title insurance, recording and other related costs;
(4) Building permits, and state and local fees;
(5) Local development impact fees;
(6) Developer Fees;
(7) Environmental hazard reports, surveys, and investigations;
(8) Reasonable carrying costs during construction, including insurance, construction
financing fees and interest, taxes, and any other expenses necessary to hold the
property while the Affordable Housing Development is under construction;
(9) Residential relocation benefits and assistance required by law;
(10) Mobilization, demolition, site preparation, and clean up;
(11) Residential construction and Rehabilitation costs;
(12) Development costs of a Unit reserved for an onsite manager, childcare, after-
school care, adult daycare, or social service and health amenities integrally
linked to, and addressing the needs of the tenants of the Restricted Units;
(13) Installation of broadband internet trunk line or fixed wireless infrastructure;
(14) Onsite improvements related to the Project;
(15) Costs related to Factory-Built Housing reservations and deposits during the
design phase;
(16) Permanent loan to pay-off construction financing related to the Project;
(17) Monitoring fees; and
(18) Any other costs of Rehabilitation or New Construction Project approved
by HDFC.
(b) Ineligible Uses of Funds
(1) Commercial Spaces. While Commercial Space may be included in a Project’s
sources and uses of funds pursuant to 4 CCR § 10322(h)(15), and Commercial
Space that qualifies as a community service facility may generate Eligible Basis
pursuant to 4 CCR § 10322(h)(33), as may be subsequently amended, HDFC
funds shall not be used for costs associated with the development, construction,
or Rehabilitation of Commercial Space within a mixed-use Project, or for a
standalone Commercial Space. Income generated from Commercial Space shall
be excluded from Project underwriting pursuant to Section 32061(a)(3).
(2) Acquisition Cost and Subdivisions. If a parcel is subdivided at or prior to closing
and a resulting parcel will be used for Market Rate or other nonresidential
purposes under separate ownership, total Acquisition costs must
be allocated proportionally based on land area and square footage. If the
Appraisal or deed reflects the Pre-Subdivision Parcel, the proposed allocation
method requires prior written approval from HDFC.
(3) Prior Owner Costs. HDFC funds shall not be used to reimburse or finance
predevelopment, Acquisition, or other Project costs incurred by any prior
unrelated ownership entities of the property, except as outlined in subsection (1)
below. Reimbursement for eligible costs is limited to actual, documented
expenses.
(A) Exemptions include directly related costs incurred by a prior owner on land
donated to develop the proposed Project, and costs incurred by the current
applicant or a previous owner that are directly related to the entitlement,
design, acquisition or development of the proposed Project. For purposes of
this exemption, “directly related” means costs that are necessary for the
Project and would not have been incurred absent the Project, such as permit
fees, architectural and engineering design expenses, environmental studies
required for approval, and acquisition costs specific to the Project site.

§ 32014. Environmental Compliance.
(a) Environmental Site Assessment (ESA)
(1) A Phase I ESA, that complies with all aspects of ASTM Standard E152, must be
completed and dated no more than 12 months prior to the application deadline.
(A) If the Phase I ESA indicates or discloses that the presence of toxic waste is
economically infeasible to remove or cannot be mitigated, then the application
is ineligible for an HDFC award.
(2) If the Phase I ESA recommends it, or indicates or discloses significant
Recognized Environmental Conditions and the Project still appears to be
feasible, a Phase II ESA must be completed and dated no more than 12 months
prior to the application deadline. If a Phase II ESA has been completed and
dated within 12 months prior to the application deadline, the originating Phase I
ESA may be dated more than 12 months prior to the application deadline.
(A) Note that many state and federal brownfield funding programs require a
Phase I ESA to be completed within 180 days prior to the close of escrow to
ensure eligibility and to establish bona fide purchaser status.
(3) Sponsor must ensure that the ESA identified environmental contamination will be
addressed in a manner that is suitable for residential development. Engaging
environmental regulatory oversight for the Project should be considered when:
(A) Environmental sampling has confirmed hazardous materials are present at
levels that are unsuitable for residential development.
(B) City or County construction permitting and entitlements required for the
Project.
(C) Hazardous materials require mitigation through engineering controls that
should be monitored in the long-term to ensure residential safety.
(D) The Project is located on or adjacent to a site listed in Department of Toxic
Substances Control’s EnviroStor [envirostor.dtsc.ca.gov] or the State Water
Resources Control Board’s GeoTracker [geotracker.waterboards.ca.gov]
databases.
(b) California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). All Projects must demonstrate
compliance with CEQA (commencing with Pub. Resources Code, §21000) prior to
initial closing or disbursement of HDFC funds, as evidenced by a valid notice of
determination, notice of exemption, or local agency statutory exemption.
(c) National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and Federal Environmental Standards.
Applicants considering federal funding sources shall comply with all applicable
federal environmental regulations, as applicable, including NEPA requirements
established at 24 CFR § 58, and, for National Housing Trust Fund assistance,
federal environmental provisions as established at 24 CFR § 93.301. Failure to
adequately comply with NEPA requirements may result in a choice-limiting action, as
defined at 24 CFR § 58.22, and may render a project ineligible for federal
assistance. Sponsors must consider environmental impacts early in the planning
process to reduce Project risk, avoid delays, and prevent choice-limiting actions.

§ 32015. Construction, Property, and Demolition Standards.
(a) Construction, Accessibility, and Energy Efficiency Standards. Sponsor shall provide
a statement that the Project meets minimum construction, accessibility, and energy
efficiency standards set forth in 4 CCR § 10325(f)(7), as may be subsequently
amended. In addition, the Sponsor shall commit to maintaining the applicable
Building Energy Efficiency Standards (California Code of Regulations, Title 24)
adopted by the California Energy Commission (CEC), as well as maintaining the
quality of installed energy efficiency, sustainability, and accessibility features when
replacing systems or materials.
(b) The Sponsor shall ensure that the construction work is performed by a licensed
general contractor with demonstrable experience in projects of similar type, scale,
and complexity. The general contractor and all subcontractors must maintain all
required licenses, certifications, and insurance required under applicable law. Work
shall be performed in compliance with applicable codes, in a competent, timely, and
professional manner and in accordance with approved plans,
(c) The Sponsor shall enter into a written construction contract with an appropriately
licensed contractor. The contract shall contain all covenants, conditions, and
representations between the parties and specify a total contract price consistent with
the HDFC approved Project budget.
(d) Demolition Restrictions
(1) Projects involving new construction that require the demolition of existing
residential Units are eligible only if the number of bedrooms in the new Project is
at least equal to the number of bedrooms in the demolished structures.
Demolished replacement Units may exist on separate parcels provided they
follow the requirements of Scattered Sites in Section (e) below.
(2) HDFC may grant an exemption when it determines the change will substantially
improve the livability of the remaining Units or serve another compelling public
policy objective (e.g., a reduction in SRO Units to add private cooking and
bathing facilities, or a reduction in public housing bedrooms necessary to meet
federal requirements).
(e) Scattered Sites
(1) All parcels will collectively constitute a single Affordable Housing Development
for purposes of these Regulations and meet the following requirements:
(A) All sites must have a single owner and Property Manager at the time of close
of escrow for HDFC financing, with the exception of any non-residential
condominium Units;
(B) The debt and associated security instruments of all Project lenders must be
the same for all sites, and multiple senior lenders shall not be allowed;
(C) Operations across all sites must be covered by a single annual report,
Schedule of Rental Income, and annual audit of the Project;
(D) HDFC must be secured against all parcels of the Project, with lien priority
relative to local public agency lenders determined in proportion to their
respective assistance amounts; and
(E) HDFC must be named as an additional insured or loss payee on all applicable
insurance policies covering all sites (including but not limited to title insurance
policies, hazard, liability, and flood insurance if applicable). Policies must
require notice to HDFC prior to any lapse in coverage or claim, and coverage
must be maintained for the full term of HDFC’s award.

§ 32016. Accessibility Standards.
(a) The Project shall meet all accessibility requirements adopted by CTCAC pursuant to
4 CCR § 10325(f)(7)(K), including for Senior Housing Type Projects as specified in 4
(b) Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 and Physical Design Accessibility
Requirements
(1) Sponsor shall comply generally with all applicable local, state, and federal
building codes and standards, as well as with all design and accessibility laws.
(2) Sponsor shall adopt written policies for providing reasonable accommodations,
reasonable modifications, and auxiliary aids and services for effective
communications with residents and applicants with Disabilities.
(3) Sponsor shall ensure that the Project is in compliance with the following housing
and building accessibility requirements as applicable:
(A) California Building Code Chapters 11A and 11B;
(B) The Fair Housing Act (42 USC § 3601 et seq.) and its implementing
regulations at 24 CFR part 100, and the ANSI A117.11986 design and
construction standard incorporated by reference at 24 CFR part 100.201a;
(C) The Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 USC § 12101 et seq.) and its
implementing regulations at 28 Code of Federal Regulations part 35 (Title II)
and part 36 (Title III);
(D) Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (29 USC § 794) and its
implementing regulations at 24 CFR part 8; and
(E) The Uniform Federal Accessibility Standards (UFAS) at 24 CFR part 40, or,
alternatively, the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design.
(c) Sponsor shall adopt and implement a written policy for providing reasonable
accommodations, reasonable modifications, and auxiliary aids and services for
effective communication with residents and applicants with disabilities. Sponsor
must provide notice in plain language and accessible formats to tenants in units with
adaptable features of their ability to request conversion of the adaptable features to
make their unit more accessible.
(d) All new and existing Projects with Accessible Housing Units shall adopt suitable
means to ensure that information regarding the availability of Accessible Housing
Units reaches eligible individuals with Disabilities and shall take reasonable
nondiscriminatory steps to maximize the utilization of such Units by eligible
individuals whose Disability requires the accessibility features of the particular unit.
Such information shall be included in marketing plans. To this end, when an
Accessible Housing Unit becomes Vacant, before offering such Unit to a household
who does not need the features of the unit, the Project shall offer such unit:
(1) First, to a current occupant of another Unit of the same Project having a
Disability requiring the accessibility features of the Vacant Unit and occupying a
Unit not having such features, or if no such occupant exists, then
(2) Second, to an Eligible Household on the waiting list having a Disability requiring
the accessibility features of the Vacant Unit.
(3) If no Eligible Household meeting the criteria in subsections (1) or (2) is available,
the Accessible Housing Unit may be offered to a tenant who does not need the
unit’s accessibility features.
(4) When offering an Accessible Housing Unit to a household that does not require
the accessibility features of the unit, the Sponsor shall require the household to
execute a lease or a lease addendum agreeing to move to a comparable non-
accessible Unit in the Project when such a Unit becomes available and an
Eligible Household requiring the features applies.
(e) For Projects with federal funds, refer to Chapter 3, Program-Specific Supplements.
(f) If a rehabilitation applicant does not propose to meet any of the requirements of
CTCAC at 4 CCR § 10325(f)(7)(A) through (I), its capital needs assessment must
show why the requirements not being met are either unnecessary or excessively

§ 32020. Eligible Applicant.
(a) An eligible applicant is a Sponsor or a Tribal Entity as described in these
Regulations.

trust, corporation, cooperative, Local Public Entity, or other legal entity, or any
combination thereof, and also includes a limited partnership in which the Sponsor or
an affiliate of the Sponsor is a general partner, which also meets the requirements of
this section, as applicable.
(c) A Sponsor shall be a Tribal Entity that meets the following:
(1) Experience. The Tribal Entity must demonstrate experience in developing,
operating, or owning at least one Affordable Rental Housing Development of
equivalent size, scope and occupancy. This may include experience of
developing, operating, or owning low-income housing projects supported by state
funds and/or Native American Housing Assistance and Self Determination Act of
1996 (NAHASDA) programs.
(A) Where a NAHASDA specific project is relied upon, the Tribal Entity may
submit the Indian Housing Block Grant Annual Allocation and Annual Report
that document the use of these funds for the low-income housing developed,
owned and operated by the Tribal Entity.
(2) Management Company. The management company must demonstrate prior
experience in operating at least one Affordable Rental Housing Development
serving a similar population to the proposed Project. If applying for Special
Needs Housing Type, Supportive Housing Type, or Farmworker Housing Type,
the Sponsor shall demonstrate that experience includes occupancy for Special
Needs households, Supportive Housing households, or Farmworker Households,
as applicable. This may include experience operating low-income housing
projects regulated by HDFC members (HCD, CalHFA) and/or NAHASDA
programs.
(A) Where a NAHASDA specific project is relied upon, the Tribal Entity may
submit the Indian Housing Block Grant Annual Allocation and Annual Report
that document the use of these funds for the low-income housing operated by
the Tribal Entity.
(d) The application requesting HDFC funds must be submitted by a Sponsor.
(e) If there are multiple Sponsors on a Project, the following requirements apply:
(1) The Co-Sponsor with experience must document that experience in the
application as required by this section.
(2) The Recipient entity must be an affiliate of the experienced Co-Sponsor directly
or indirectly controlled by the experienced Co-Sponsor, in accordance with the
control standards defined in these Regulations, continuously from the time of
award through the full term of the HDFC documents.
(f) Experience Requirements. Sponsor and management company eligibility, except for
Tribal Entities, is based on demonstrated experience. Furthermore, Sponsor is
evaluated under two classifications: Established Developer or Emerging Developer.
(1) Sponsor Experience
(A) An Established Developer Sponsor shall demonstrate:
1. Completion of 5 or more affordable housing projects subject to public
agency affordability, occupancy, and/or rent restrictions placed in service
for at least 3 years;
2. Each project contains at least 10 Units,
3. At least 2 projects are regulated by HDFC, HCD, CalHFA, or CTCAC; and
4. At least 1 project serves the similar population as the population identified
in the HDFC Housing Type for the proposed Project. If applying for
Special Needs Housing Type, Supportive Housing Project Type, or
Farmworker Housing Type; the Sponsor shall demonstrate that
experience includes occupancy for Special Needs Households, Supportive
Housing Households, or Farmworker Households, as applicable.
(B) An Emerging Developer Sponsor shall demonstrate:
1. Completion of at least 1 but no more than 4 projects in service for at least
3 years; completed within 10 years of the date of application
a. Emerging Developer Sponsor may use projects that were developed at
other firms if it meets the requirements under subsection (d), Qualifying
Prior Experience below.
2. Each project contains at least 10 Units, and
3. At least 1 project is regulated by HDFC, HCD, CalHFA or CTCAC.
4. Qualifying Prior Experience
a. HDFC may recognize Affordable Housing Development experience
obtained by an individual who serves or served previously as a
Development Manager, Senior Development Manager, Project
Manager, Senior Project Manager, Director of Development, Vice
President of Development, or other comparable position, provided the
individual exercised substantial responsibility for planning, financing,
entitlements, development, construction, Rehabilitation, or successful
completion of the project(s) that is being used for qualifying experience
purposes.
b. HDFC may require documentation to verify material participation in the
qualifying projects at HDFC’s discretion.
c. Experience credited under this subsection may only be used if HDFC
determines the individual exercised primary responsibility for significant
development activities and not merely administrative, consulting, or
support functions.
(2) Management Company Experience.
(A) The management company, proposed for the Project, except for Projects
proposed by Tribal Entities, must demonstrate:
1. Experience managing 6 or more projects placed in service for at least 3
years;
2. At least 2 projects regulated by HDFC, HCD, CalHFA or CTCAC; and
3. At least 2 of which must have served the similar population identified in
the Housing Type as the proposed Project. If applying as a Special Needs
Housing Type, Supportive Housing Type, or Farmworker Housing Type,
the Sponsor shall demonstrate that Property Manager experience includes
occupancy for Special Needs Households, Supportive Housing
Households, or Farmworker Households, as applicable.
(B) If the management company will be the Emerging Developer for which the
project receives Sponsor experience, the Sponsor shall contract with a
management company meeting all minimum management company
experience cited in subsection (1) above, for at least three years following the
date placed in service.
(g) Capacity Requirements. Sponsor and management company eligibility, except for
Tribal Entities, is based on demonstrated capacity.
(1) Sponsor Capacity. The Sponsor must demonstrate sufficient organizational,
financial, and operational capacity to own and develop the proposed project.
Sponsors with significant or unresolved capacity concerns may be deemed
ineligible.
(A) Established Developer Sponsor. An Established Developer Sponsor must
provide evidence of financial stability. For-profit developers must provide
evidence acceptable to HDFC of growing cash and equivalents and positive
net income for the past three years. Non-profit developers must provide
evidence acceptable to HDFC of growing cash and equivalents and positive
change in net assets over the past three years.

whether the Emerging Developer applies as the sole Sponsor or partners with
an eligible Established Developer as a joint venture.
1. Sole Sponsor.

HDFC including but not limited to a balance sheet and income
statement for at least one but no more than three years for the
Sponsor. A rent roll and operating statement in a form acceptable to
HDFC must also be provided for each project the Sponsor has
developed as of fiscal year end for at least one but no more than three
years.
b. Sponsor shall provide resumes for all key development team members
demonstrating demonstrable experience in planning, financing, and
completing affordable housing projects of comparable type, scale, and
complexity to the proposed Project.

(i) 1 Project until after construction loan closing for the Project; and
(ii) No more than 2 concurrent Projects until after Permanent Loan

which the Emerging Developer Sponsor participates pursuant to a
Joint Venture arrangement.
2. Joint venture with an Established Developer Sponsor. Joint venture

a. The Established Developer Sponsor must allocate at least 40% of the

completion or permanent financing close of escrow (whichever is

ownership interest in the Project for a minimum of 5 years following the
date the project is placed in Service. Right of first refusal for purchase
option must to be provided to the Emerging Developer; and
c. Both parties must submit a draft memorandum of understanding
outlining the roles and responsibilities sufficient to demonstrate
adequate capacity, as determined by HDFC. The draft MOU must be
executed by the time of loan closing.
d. Both parties must submit the above documentation in subsection
2(a)(i) and (ii) above to confirm capacity.
(2) Management Company Financial Capacity. The proposed management
company must provide evidence acceptable to HDFC of growing cash and
equivalents and positive net income for the past three years.
(3) Prior Performance. In evaluating Sponsor eligibility and organizational capacity,
HDFC may consider the Sponsor’s prior performance history in accordance with
Section 32098.

§ 32041. Tie-Breakers.
If two or more applications are awarded the same total number of points, HDFC shall
apply a formal tie-breaker methodology. Applications shall be ranked by the highest
public benefit per dollar of cost-adjusted requests.
(a) A Project’s public benefit is the sum of all of the following:
(1) The Project’s rent savings benefit, which is as follows:
(A) For all Projects not covered in subsection (B), the product of the sum across
all Restricted Units of each unit’s difference between the monthly fair market
rent established by HUD for the County in which the Project is located and the
Area Median Income monthly gross rent limit for that Unit at the targeted rent
level for the appropriate bedroom size, all calculated according to the
methodology for tax credit rents, multiplied by 180. If this calculation results in
a negative number for any particular unit, then the rent savings benefit for that
Unit shall not be lower than zero. Units with federal project-based rental
assistance or a similar local rental assistance program approved by the
Executive Director shall be assigned targeted rent levels the greater of actual
rent targeting or 30% AMI. If the average affordability of Restricted Units,
exclusive of units with rental assistance, is less than 40% AMI, then the
calculation shall assume a targeted rent level of 40% AMI for each tax credit
unit that does not have rental assistance.
(B) For Acquisition/Rehabilitation Projects whose actual rents are less than the
CTCAC rent limits, the sum of the following: (a) for Restricted Units without
federal project-based rental assistance or a similar local rental assistance
program approved by the HDFC Executive Director, the product of the sum
across all such Units of each Unit’s difference between the monthly fair
market rent established by HUD for the county in which the Project is located
and the average rent charged for each Unit over the last three years, as
documented with rent rolls or property audits, multiplied by 180. If this
calculation results in a negative number for any particular unit, then the rent
savings benefit for that Unit shall not be lower than zero.
(2) The Project’s population benefit, which is comprised of a Very Low-Income (VLI)
benefit and a special populations benefit.
(A) The VLI benefit is the product of the number of Restricted Units targeted at
50% of AMI or below multiplied by 180. Units with federal project-based rental
assistance or a similar local rental assistance program approved by the
Executive Director shall be assigned targeted rent levels the greater of actual
rent targeting or 30% AMI. If the average affordability of Restricted Units,
exclusive of units with rental assistance, is less than 40% AMI, then the
calculation shall assume a targeted rent level of 40% AMI for each tax credit
unit that does not have rental assistance. The VLI benefit is calculated as
follows:
1. A benefit for the product of the number of Restricted Units targeted at 30%
of AMI or below multiplied by $1,250.
2. A benefit for the product of the number of Restricted Units targeted at 35%
of AMI or below multiplied by $1,000.
3. A benefit for the product of the number of Restricted Units targeted at 40%
of AMI or below multiplied by $750.
4. A benefit for the product of the number of Restricted Units targeted at 45%
of AMI or below multiplied by $500.
5. A benefit for the product of the number of Restricted Units targeted at 50%
of AMI or below multiplied by $250.
(B) The special populations benefit is the product of the number of Restricted
Units restricted to Special Needs Populations, or Farmworkers, as defined in
Section 34000 of these Regulations, multiplied by the factors listed as follows
below, and limited to no more than 50% of Restricted Units:
1. A benefit for the product of the number of Restricted Units dedicated to
Special Needs Populations multiplied by $100,000. Eligible to Projects
with fewer than 25% of the Restricted Units dedicated to Special Needs
Populations. Units receiving this special populations benefit are subject to
supportive services requirements per Section 32100.
2. A benefit for the product of the number of Restricted Units dedicated to
Special Needs Populations multiplied by $300,000. Eligible to Projects that
restrict 25% or more of the Restricted Units to Special Needs Populations.
Units receiving this special populations benefit are subject to supportive
services requirements per Section 32100.
3. Farmworkers multiplied by $50,000.
(3) The Project’s location benefit, which is comprised of a Resource Area benefit, a
Community Revitalization Area benefit, a Community-Based Developer benefit
and a Greenhouse Gas Reduction benefit. If a Project is eligible for both a
Resource Area benefit and a Community Revitalization Area benefit, the Sponsor
shall select only one of these benefits. The Resource Area benefit and
Community Revitalization Area benefit shall not be additive.
(A) The Resource Area benefit is one of the following:
1. The product of the bedroom-adjusted number of Restricted Units, using
the current CDLAC tie-breaker adjustment factors pursuant to CDLAC
regulations 4 CCR § 5106(f), as may be subsequently amended in a Large
Family, Special Needs, Supportive Housing, or High Density Housing
Project per Section 32040(b) located in a Highest Resource Area as
specified on the CTCAC/HCD Opportunity Area Map multiplied by
2. The product of the bedroom-adjusted number of Restricted Units in a
Large Family, Special Needs, Supportive Housing, or High Density
Housing Project per Section 32040(b) located in a High Resource Area as
specified on the CTCAC/HCD Opportunity Area Map multiplied by
3. The product of the bedroom-adjusted number of Restricted Units in a
Large Family, Special Needs, Supportive Housing, or High Density
Housing Project per Section 32040(b) located in a Moderate Resource
Area as specified on the CTCAC/HCD Opportunity Area Map multiplied by
$10,000. A Sponsor may choose to utilize the census tract or census block
group resource designation from the CTCAC/HCD Opportunity Maps in
effect when the initial site control was obtained up to seven calendar years
prior to the application.
4. The product of the bedroom-adjusted number of Restricted Units in a new
construction or Acquisition/Rehabilitation Project located in neighborhoods
identified as experiencing neighborhood change as specified on the HCD
Neighborhood Change Map multiplied by $30,000.
5. A Project is ineligible for this benefit if it receives a Community
Revitalization Area benefit.
(B) The Community Revitalization Area benefit is the product of the bedroom-
adjusted number of Restricted Units that are located in a Community
Revitalization Area and are a component in the Area’s Community
Revitalization Plan multiplied by $20,000. A Project is ineligible for this benefit
if it receives a Resource Area benefit.
(C) The Community-Based Developer benefit is the product of the bedroom-
adjusted number of Restricted Units multiplied by $20,000, for applications
submitted by Community-Based Developers. A Project is ineligible for this

Restricted Units multiplied by $20,000, for applications submitted by Tribal

(4) The Greenhouse Gas Reduction benefit applies to Projects that have requested

§ 32067. Sponsor Financial Capacity Metrics.
(a) HDFC shall establish baseline financial-capacity metrics to evaluate Sponsor
organizational health, inform underwriting risk management, determine eligibility for
funding at construction, and support post-award asset management. This data
collection further informs HDFC’s broader understanding of financial capacity across
the sector, helping HDFC evaluate systemic stress and identify paths towards long-
term stability in furtherance of its mission.
(b) Application Submission and Completeness. Every Sponsor applying for HDFC
awards shall submit self-certified financial-capacity metrics as part of its application
for funding. Submission of the required metrics is required solely to deem the
application complete for underwriting review. These metrics shall not serve as an
application threshold requirement under Article 2, nor shall they be used to
competitively score, rank, or disqualify an application for an HDFC award. A Sponsor
shall not receive additional points or competitive preference for exceeding minimum
financial thresholds, nor shall a Sponsor be penalized in application scoring or award
selection for reporting metrics below the minimum financial threshold.
(1) To satisfy the application completion requirement, Sponsor shall submit a
completed Sponsor Financial Capacity Schedule executed by an authorized
corporate officer under penalty of perjury. Except as provided in subsection (c)(3)
below, for the purposes of this section, HDFC shall not require the submission of
audited financial statements, tax returns, bank statements, or CPA certifications,
or other supporting documentation to verify Sponsor’s self-reported metrics at the
time of application.
(2) Each applicant shall also provide as part of their submission the number of years
they have been in operation and the number of units in their portfolio.
(c) Self-Certification and Investigation
(1) Financial capacity metrics shall be self-certified by an authorized representative
of the Sponsor in the form and manner prescribed by HDFC.
(2) Nothing in this Section limits HDFC’s authority to request supporting
documentation or investigate circumstances where HDFC has reason to believe
that information submitted by a Sponsor is materially false, misleading, or
incomplete.
(d) Required Financial Capacity Metrics. Sponsors shall report corporate and portfolio
metrics using uniform calculation methodologies prescribed by HDFC, including:
(1) Corporate Liquidity (Unrestricted Cash and Cash Equivalents). Corporate or
parent-level Unrestricted cash and cash equivalents as of the Fiscal Year-end for
each of the 3 most recently completed Fiscal Years. Sponsor shall report the
absolute dollar amount for each year so that both the level and trend of liquidity
can be evaluated. The minimum threshold for this metric is a greater amount of
cash and equivalents at the end of year three than at the end of year one.
(2) Corporate Liquidity (Days Cash and Cash Equivalents). Corporate or parent-level
days cash and cash equivalents as of fiscal year end for each of the 3 most
recently completed fiscal years, using a uniform calculation methodology
prescribed by HDFC. The minimum threshold for this metric is at least 180 days
of cash and equivalents for each year reported.
(3) Portfolio Health – Economic Occupancy. Median economic occupancy across the
Sponsor’s portfolio at Fiscal Year-end for each of the 3 most recently completed
fiscal years. The minimum threshold for this metric is at least 90 percent
economic occupancy for each year reported.
(4) Portfolio Health – Debt Service Coverage. Median Debt Service Coverage Ratios
across the Sponsor’s portfolio at Fiscal Year-end for each of the 3 most recently
completed Fiscal Years, expressed in 1.xx form. The minimum threshold for this
metric is a median portfolio debt service coverage ratio of at least 1.10 for each
year reported.
(5) Portfolio Health and Parent-Level Portfolio Support. The annual dollar amount of
cash support provided at the corporate or parent level to each Project, together
with the total amount of parent-level support provided to the total portfolio during
that year for each of the last 3 years. The threshold for this metric is no more
than five percent of the prior year’s cash and equivalents provided to the total
portfolio for each year reported.
(e) Sponsors with Limited Operating History
(1) A Sponsor with fewer than 3 completed fiscal years shall report available data for
each completed fiscal year.
(2) A Sponsor that does not own or control an operating housing portfolio via a
Sponsor affiliate shall indicate portfolio metrics as not applicable.
(3) A Sponsor shall not be deemed outside of an acceptable range solely because it
is an Emerging Developer as defined in these Regulations, has fewer than three
(3) years of operating history, or lacks an existing operating portfolio.
(f) Acceptable Thresholds. These minimal thresholds shall not constitute competitive
scoring criteria.
(g) Financial Capacity Plan
(1) A Sponsor whose reported metrics do not meet any one of the minimum
thresholds shall submit a written financial plan as a condition of award
acceptance, unless the Sponsor chooses to form a joint venture per subsection
(h)(2) below.
(2) HDFC shall identify the specific metrics requiring a plan but shall not prescribe a
mandatory template. The Sponsor shall determine the form and substance of the
plan, explaining the circumstances and the specific corrective actions taken or
proposed.
(3) The financial plan must be signed by the Chief Executive Officer and the Chair of
the Board of Directors or equivalent presiding officer of the Sponsor’s governing
board.
(4) HDFC’s receipt of a financial capacity plan satisfies the relevant aspect of
application completeness, but shall not constitute HDFC approval, endorsement,
or representation regarding the effectiveness of the plan or the Sponsor’s
financial solvency.
(h) Eligibility For HDFC Funds During Construction
(1) A Sponsor is eligible for funding during construction only if its reported financial
capacity metrics satisfy each of the acceptable threshold minimums.
(2) A Sponsor with metrics below any of the minimum thresholds will be eligible for
HDFC construction phase financing if the Sponsor chooses to form a joint
venture partnership with a Sponsor who meets all required minimum threshold
requirements.
(3) Ineligibility for funding during construction shall not, by itself, disqualify a Sponsor
from receiving an HDFC award or utilizing permanent financing provided by
HDFC.
(4) HDFC may, in its sole discretion, restore a Sponsor’s eligibility for funding during
construction prior to disbursement if the Sponsor demonstrates that its metrics
have returned to acceptable ranges.
(i) Post-Award Monitoring
(1) If a Sponsor required to submit a financial capacity plan receives an HDFC
Award, the plan shall become part of HDFC’s asset-management and loan-
monitoring process.
(2) Following loan and grant closing, the Sponsor shall submit an updated financial
capacity plan signed by its board chair annually until HDFC determines, in its
sole discretion, that the Sponsor’s metrics have remained within acceptable
ranges for a sufficient period.
(j) Anonymized Industry Reporting. HDFC shall publish aggregated and anonymized
data derived from the metrics collected under this section on its website not less
than annually. Published data shall not identify individual Sponsors, Projects, or
affiliates, and shall be formatted to prevent individual identification.
(k) These metrics will be required annually and not with each application if more than
one application is submitted in a calendar year.
(l) Nothing in this section shall be interpreted to convert financial capacity metrics into
competitive scoring criteria or to favor any Sponsor.

(10) Sponsor and Recipient (if applicable), shall submit to HDFC an authorizing
resolution accompanied by an attorney opinion letter that provides legal confirmation
regarding the Sponsor and if applicable, the borrower’s authority, due execution, and
enforceability of the loan/grant documents, to the satisfaction of the Executive
Director.
(c) Funding at Conversion to Permanent Financing Only
(1) For Projects awarded permanent financing only, HDFC does not disburse HDFC
state funds during the construction period. HDFC funds are held until the
following:
(A) All items under Section 32090(b) must be met.
(B) HDFC state funds may be sent to escrow for the Permanent Loan Closing
when the Recipient submits an accurate, completed and executed audited
cost certification and HDFC disbursement request form to HDFC no less than
45 days prior to the close of escrow. The funds must remain in escrow until
HDFC authorizes release of the HDFC funds to the Recipient.
(C) No retention applies to HDFC state funds disbursed under this Permanent
Loan Closing payment.
(d) Funding During Construction
(1) HDFC’s construction disbursement structure is intended to operate until
CalHFA’s construction lending program is established, at which time HDFC will
coordinate with CalHFA to ensure alignment.
(2) Two-Phase Construction Disbursement Structure. HDFC construction
disbursements shall consist of both: (A) an initial advance at construction
financing closing and (B) a completion advance at Project Completion. HDFC
shall not administer periodic construction draws between the initial advance and
project completion except as provided for in subsection (C) below.
(A) Initial Advance
1. Eligibility. To receive an initial advance, the Project must have received an
HDFC award and an allocation of federal tax credits (LIHTC), and the
Recipient must satisfy HDFC’s Financial-Capacity Metrics as described in
Section 32067.
2. Amount. The initial advance shall equal the total HDFC award multiplied
by the initial advance percentage of the tax credit investor’s initial capital
contribution. For example, if the investor’s initial capital contribution made
at construction loan closing equals 10% of the investor’s total investment,
then HDFC’s initial advice of loan proceeds made at construction loan
closing shall equal 10% of the total HDFC loan.
3. Conditions. The initial advance is conditioned solely upon satisfaction of
the Financial-Capacity Metrics, execution and where applicable,
recordation of all required HDFC documents, concurrent closing of the
primary construction loan, concurrent funding of the initial tax credit equity
contribution, and the absence of any known uncured material default
under the HDFC documents.
4. Reliance and Efficiency. HDFC shall publish a standardized checklist of
required closing documents to disburse at construction closing. To
eliminate duplicative review, HDFC may rely on closing statements,
inspections, title policies, and certifications prepared or accepted by the
construction lender, tax credit investor, local jurisdiction, or escrow holder.
(B) Completion Advance
1. Project Completion. For purposes of this section, “Completion” shall mean
the occurrence of physical construction completion as evidenced by
documentation including but not limited to a copy of a temporary certificate
of occupancy, certificate of occupancy, an architect’s certificate of
substantial completion, and other equivalent documents acceptable to
HDFC in its sole and absolute discretion.
2. Disbursement at Completion. Upon Completion, HDFC shall disburse the
remaining balance of the HDFC award directly into escrow, in an amount
determined in part by the senior construction lender’s payment demand,
for the sole purpose of paying down the construction loan. Such funds
shall not be disbursed directly to the Recipient. Disbursement shall not be
conditioned upon lease up, permanent loan conversion, tax credit capital
contributions at conversion or upon issuance of LIHTC Form 8609, or
formal Permanent Loan Closing.
(C) Exclusions. This two-phase disbursement structure shall not apply to funding
that HCD has historically provided during construction period:
1. Awards of HOME and NHTF funds awarded by HCD,
2. Awards of IIG and Serna funds administered by HDFC, or
3. Any other program where HDFC determines, in its sole discretion, that
applying this structure would violate statutory mandates or jeopardize
Project funding.
(D) Disbursement Procedures for Excluded Programs. The following procedures
are applicable to the excluded programs described in Section 32090(d)(2)(C)
above.
1. HDFC funds may be sent to escrow for the construction closing when the
Recipient submits an accurate, completed and executed HDFC
disbursement request form and supporting documentation for eligible
costs to HDFC no less than 45 days prior to the planned date to close
escrow. The funds must remain in escrow until HDFC authorizes release
of the HDFC funds to the Recipient.
2. HDFC funds must be disbursed for eligible costs, less a retention amount
not to exceed 5% of the total HDFC loan/grant amount, as determined by
HDFC in its sole discretion, pursuant to Civ. Code, § 8811, unless HDFC
releases retention in order to expend the funds prior to a statutory and/or
regulatory expenditure deadline. The retention amount, less applicable
cost savings, will be released at conversion to permanent financing. The
COSR grant amount is not included in the calculation of the retention.
3. HDFC funds may be wired to escrow for the Permanent Loan Closing
when the Recipient submits an accurate, completed and executed audited
cost certification and HDFC disbursement request form to HDFC no less
than 30 days prior to the close of escrow. The funds must remain in
escrow until HDFC authorizes release of the HDFC funds to the Recipient.
4. If, upon completion of construction, the total development funding sources
exceed the total development costs, HDFC may, after re-underwriting the
project and revising the funding layering review, reduce the amount of the
HDFC award provided in the Award Commitment Letter on a pro-rata
basis. HDFC may reallocate the cost savings in the following manner but
not limited to: use for future funding awards or directly fund a Project with
existing HDFC financing that is under construction and has a financing
gap due to cost overruns or other circumstances approved by HDFC.
(e) Cost Savings at Permanent Loan Conversion. If, upon permanent loan conversion,
total development funding sources exceed total actual development costs, HDFC
may reduce the amount of the HDFC award provided in the Award Commitment

§ 32094. Rent Increase Limitation.
(a) Rent Increase Limitation
(1) For all Projects, annual gross rent increases for Restricted Units shall not exceed
the rent increase limitation established and published annually by CTCAC,
including any exceptions provided in the CTCAC regulations. Any adjustment to
the CTCAC limit shall automatically apply.
(2) Sponsors shall comply with all applicable state and federal rent limitation laws,
including local rent control ordinances where applicable.
(3) The rent increase limitations established in this section are subject to the
applicable program-specific requirements set forth in Chapter 3, which shall
control in the event of any conflict.
(b) Tribal Housing Projects
(1) For Tribal Housing Projects, as defined in Section 32040(b)(1)(F), HDFC shall
apply this section with maximum feasible flexibility, consistent with Health & Saf.
Code, § 54931(q)(3). HDFC shall not impose rent increase limitations or related
administrative requirements in a manner inconsistent with Tribal sovereignty or
federal law. HDFC may approve alternative rent increase structures for Tribal
Housing Projects provided the alternative does not violate state law, or federal
statutory or regulatory requirements.
(c) Waiver
(1) For Projects subject to a CTCAC regulatory agreement, HDFC shall defer to
CTCAC's determination on rent increase limit waiver requests. A separate
waiver request to HDFC is not required for co-funded Projects where CTCAC
has approved the waiver, consistent with the CTCAC Rent Increase Limit Waiver
Memorandum, or any successor guidance, as published on the CTCAC website.
(2) For Projects not subject to a CTCAC regulatory agreement, the Executive
Director may grant a waiver to exceed the rent increase limit if the Sponsor
demonstrates that the proposed increase is necessary to ensure the financial
stability or Fiscal Integrity of the property and does not unreasonably impact the
tenants. The Executive Director shall establish and publish the process and
criteria for waiver requests.
(3) A waiver denial is subject to the appeals process described in Section 32087.
(d) Notice
(1) For Projects subject to a CTCAC regulatory agreement, owners shall comply
with the tenant notice requirements established by CTCAC under 4 CCR §
10336(a)(3), including the notice required under Civ. Code, § 827. For Projects
not subject to a CTCAC regulatory agreement, Sponsor shall provide written
notice of any rent increase in accordance with Civ. Code, § 827. The notice must
state the amount of the increase, the new rent, the applicable rent increase limit,
and the effective date, in plain, accessible language. The notice must include the
name, telephone number, and email address of a representative who can
answer the tenant's questions about the increase.
(e) Annual Rent Limitation Review
(1) Annually, and in coordination with CTCAC's annual assessment required under
AB 846 (Ch. 674, Statutes of 2024), the Executive Director shall review the rent
increase limitation established under this section to confirm continued alignment
with CTCAC's published limit and evaluate its impact on the HDFC portfolio. The
Executive Director may recommend adjustments to the HDFC Executive
Committee based on that review. Any adjustment adopted by the HDFC
Executive Committee shall be published and take effect for the following
calendar year.

to such remedies as HDFC determines appropriate in its sole discretion,
consistent with the HDFC documents and applicable law.
(g) Restricted Units Assisted with Rental Subsidy Programs

Part 982) or other similar rental assistance, the rules of the rental assistance
program pertaining to rent increases shall prevail for as long as the rental
assistance remains in place. Changes in the tenant contribution amounts may
occur more often than annually, as required by the rental assistance program.
HDFC will defer to the subsidy program to set rents and determine the tenant-
paid portion.

§ 32095. Fair Housing, Tenant Protections, and Tenant Selection.
The Sponsor must comply with all applicable local, state, and federal laws,
constitutions, codes, standards, rules, guidelines, and regulations, including, without
limitation, those that pertain to accessibility, construction, health and safety, labor, fair
housing, fair employment practices, affirmatively further fair housing, nondiscrimination,
and equal opportunity. In addition, Sponsor must do all the following:
(a) Nondiscrimination policy. Adopt a written nondiscrimination policy requiring that no
person, on the basis of any protected class under federal or state Fair Housing
Laws, including race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender
expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial
status, source of income, disability, age, medical condition, genetic information,
citizenship, primary language, immigration status (except where prohibited by
federal law), criminal history, arbitrary characteristics, perceived membership in a
protected class, record of membership in a protected class, or association with a
protected class, be excluded from participation in, denied benefits of, or subjected to
discrimination under any HDFC funding program or activity receiving tax credits and
bonds.
Affirmative Fair Housing Marketing Plan. Develop and implement an affirmative fair
housing marketing plan. Such plan shall be consistent with the Fair Housing Act, 42
USC § 3601 et seq. and consistent with HUD’s equal opportunity regulations at 24
CFR part 200, subpart M.
(b) Accessible Housing Units. All new and existing projects with Accessible Housing
Units shall adopt a process to market information about these Units to eligible
individuals with Disabilities and take reasonable, nondiscriminatory steps to
maximize their use by individuals who require accessibility features. When an
Accessible Housing Unit becomes Vacant, the owner or Property Manager shall
offer the unit: First, to a current occupant of another Unit in the same Project, or in a
comparable Project under common control, who has a Disability requiring the
accessibility features of the Vacant Unit and is occupying a Unit without those
features, including, but not limited to, adaptable Units; Units with audio and visual
assistance; and all Units meeting the latest adopted California Building Codes and
standards, and Americans with Disabilities Act standards; or, if no such occupant
exists, then Second, to an eligible, qualified tenant applicant on the waiting list who
has a Disability requiring the accessibility features of the Vacant Unit, as defined by
the latest adopted California Building Codes and standards, and Americans with
Disabilities Act standards. If no tenant meeting the criteria in the above subsections
(1) or (2) is available, the Accessible Housing Unit may be offered to a tenant who
does not require the unit’s accessibility features. When offering an Accessible
Housing Unit to a tenant who does not require its accessibility features, the owner or
Property Manager shall require the tenant to agree to move to a non-accessible Unit
when a comparable Unit becomes available. This agreement shall be incorporated
into the lease or a lease addendum.
(c) Reasonable Accommodation. Adopt and implement a written policy for providing
reasonable accommodations, reasonable modifications, and auxiliary aids and
services, as defined by the American Disability Act, and any enhanced accessibility
features of the property or unit, to ensure effective communication with residents and
Sponsors with Disabilities. Sponsor must provide notice, in plain language and
accessible formats, to tenants in Units with adaptable features of their ability to
request conversion of those features to make the Unit more accessible.
(d) Violence Against Women Act (VAWA). Where applicable, ensure that individuals are
not denied assistance, evicted, or have their assistance terminated because they are
survivors of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, or stalking, or
because they are affiliated with a victim, pursuant to 34 USC § 12491. Sponsor must
inform prospective and current tenants of their rights under federal law by providing
the Notice of Occupancy Rights (Form HUD-5380) and the VAWA Self-Certification
(Form HUD-5382). Notice must be provided when a person is denied housing, when
admitted to housing, and when a tenant is notified of eviction or termination. Sponsor
and Property Managers must also comply with additional protections under state
law, including Civ. Code, § 1946.7 (early lease termination without penalty) and Civ.
(e) Tenant Selection Policy. Adopt a written tenant selection policy, in clear, intelligible,
and unambiguous language, that complies with state and federal law, includes Fair
Housing Laws, and is consistent with the Project’s Housing Type requirements in
Section 32040 (b). The tenant selection policy must include how accessibility needs
are addressed for any populations with Disabilities or exiting institutions. Tenant
selection must be described in the management plan required in Section 32100
(1) For Special Needs and Supportive Housing Types:
(A) The tenant selection policy must include Housing First requirements in Welf.
& Inst. Code, § 8255.
(B) Referrals shall be made through the Coordinated Entry System or a
comparable prioritization and/or referral system based on greatest need. If
referrals will be made using a prioritization system other than CES, the
Sponsor must describe the plan for tenant referrals in detail, including which

prioritization process.
(f) Waiting List Due to Disasters. Sponsors and Property Manager shall comply with
any federal, state, or local laws, rules or policies that require a tenant waitlist priority
for households displaced and experiencing Homelessness due to a Presidentially
declared disaster under the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency
Assistance Act (42 USC § 5121 et seq.) or State of Emergency declared by the
Governor of California in accordance with the State of California Constitution and
California Emergency Services Act (Gov. Code, § 8550 et seq.).
(g) Tenant Grievance and Appeal Procedure. Unless required by another federal, state,
or local program, adopt a tenant grievance and appeal procedure to resolve
grievances filed by tenants and appeals of adverse actions taken by Sponsor or
managers regarding occupancy of a Low-Income Unit or applications for occupancy.
(1) The grievance and appeal procedure shall be subject to HDFC review upon
request and shall, at a minimum, include:
(A) A requirement to provide each tenant and Sponsor with a written copy of the
grievance and appeal procedure;
(B) Procedures for informal dispute resolution;
(C) A right to a hearing before an impartial body consisting of one or more
persons with the authority to render a final decision on the appeal or
grievance; and
(D) Procedures for conducting an appeal or grievance hearing and for appointing

(2) Neither use of, nor participation in any of the appeal and grievance procedures

Saf. Code, § 50466).

§ 32099. Roles of Reviewing Entities.
(a) HDFC as Lead Monitoring Entity. HDFC is the lead entity responsible for ongoing
compliance and long-term monitoring of Projects funded under the programs it
administers. HDFC holds the Regulatory Agreement, oversees compliance with
these Regulations and the loan/grant documents, and serves as the primary point of
decision for compliance and asset management matters throughout the term of the
affordability and funding obligations.
(b) Coordinated Monitoring for Co-Regulated Projects. Many Projects receive funding or
allocations from more than one reviewing entity, including HDFC, CTCAC, CDLAC,
CalHFA, and HCD. For these co-regulated Projects, HDFC shall coordinate ongoing
compliance and monitoring with the other reviewing entities consistent with AB 179
and any memorandum of understanding or successor agreement among the
reviewing entities. The goals of this coordination are to ensure that a single entity
conducts physical inspections of a Project, to eliminate duplicate submissions, and
to align the processes for obtaining required approvals, including reserve draws,
ownership changes, property management changes, operating budgets, and capital
needs assessments. HDFC may enter into, modify, and implement agreements with
the other reviewing entities to carry out this coordination as the roles of the reviewing
entities evolve.
(c) Federal Grantee Responsibilities. For Projects receiving HOME or NHTF funds,
HCD retains the grantee responsibilities and oversight obligations required under 24
CFR Parts 92 and 93. Coordination with other reviewing entities under this section
does not delegate, diminish, or transfer HCD’s responsibilities to HUD, and HCD
remains responsible for ensuring ongoing compliance with applicable federal
requirements.
(d) Division of Responsibilities. The reviewing entities may allocate ongoing compliance
and monitoring responsibilities among themselves as appropriate to each Project's
funding sources and regulatory agreements. These responsibilities include, but are
not limited to, annual reporting, audited financial statements, operating budget
review, reserve disbursement approvals, physical inspections, occupancy and
income compliance, and review of ownership and management changes. HDFC
may rely on the monitoring, inspections, or determinations of another reviewing
entity where appropriate, and may establish the documentation and reporting
required to support that reliance. Allocation of responsibilities under this section
does not relieve a Sponsor of any obligation under the loan documents, the
applicable regulatory agreements, or applicable law.

§ 32110. Required Legal Documents.
(a) Award Commitment Letter. Upon awarding HDFC funds to a Project, HDFC shall

legal and regulatory obligations, construction and disbursement requirements,
schedules and budgets, reporting and monitoring responsibilities, relocation and
publicity requirements, available remedies, and any authorized Tribal Entity waivers.
(1) If the Recipient of the funds is not the Sponsor, the agreement(s) shall require a
guaranty securing the Sponsor’s specific performance of all contractual
requirements associated with the awarded program funds. The guaranty is not a
repayment guaranty.
(b) Loan Documents. Prior to disbursement of any loan funds, the Recipient must enter
into the following HDFC loan documents:
(1) Promissory Note and Deed of Trust. All HDFC loans shall be evidenced by a
promissory note payable to HDFC, stating the principal amount of the loan and
the loan terms required under the applicable program. The note shall be secured
by a deed of trust encumbering all sites comprising the Project property, naming
HDFC as beneficiary or, for Tribal Entities, by other security acceptable to HDFC.
The deed of trust or other approved security instruments shall be recorded and
shall be junior only to such liens, encumbrances and other matters of record
approved by HDFC subject to Section 32112 of these Regulations. This security
shall secure HDFC’s financial interest in the Project and ensure specific
performance of the Recipient’s obligations subject to applicable California law.
(2) Affordability Agreement
(A) For all HDFC loans, HDFC shall enter into an affordability agreement with the
Recipient for a term not less than the original term of the loan. The HDFC
affordability agreement shall be recorded in first position ahead of any and all
liens that include foreclosure remedies. It is not required to be senior in
priority to any regulatory agreements or similar documents that do not grant
foreclosure remedies.
(B) The affordability agreement shall include only those terms necessary to
ensure that the Project remains restricted to the same affordability level for all
occupants, rents or amounts charged pursuant thereto, reporting
requirements not related to tenant occupancy and affordability, and level of
operations and maintenance.
(C) If project based rental assistance is terminated, the affordability agreement
may permit rents to increase only to the minimum extent necessary to
maintain fiscal integrity; however, in no event shall rents exceed 30% of 60%
of AMI, as determined by HUD and adjusted for unit size using TCAC’s
annually published income limits and maximum rents.

the Recipient for a term not less than the original term of the loan. The HDFC
Regulatory Agreement shall be recorded in the official records of the county
where the Project is located, against the property prior to the disbursement of
funds. The HDFC Regulatory Agreement shall include, but not be limited to all
terms, conditions, obligations, and restrictions applicable to the Project based on
the program(s) from which it receives funding. Such terms may address
requirements related to the Project as a whole, Restricted Units, tenant selection,
rental and occupancy agreement provisions, unit mix, operating and
management standards, reserve accounts, sponsor distributions, reporting and
oversight, property maintenance, enforcement mechanisms, successor
obligations, special conditions of award, and any other provisions necessary to
ensure full compliance with all applicable program requirements.

by the State of California to authorize the transfer of funds. This may include
standard 213/215 forms or any other state-approved disbursement forms

into the following HDFC grant documents:

recorded in the official records of the county where the Project is located, against
the property prior to the disbursement of funds. The HDFC covenant shall
include, but is not limited to all terms, conditions, obligations, and restrictions
applicable to the Project based on the program(s) from which it receives funding.

selection, rental and occupancy agreement provisions, unit mix, operating and
management standards, reserve accounts, sponsor distributions, reporting and
oversight, property maintenance, enforcement mechanisms, successor

the manner, timing, and conditions under which grant funds will be disbursed,
and it must be fully executed before any grant funds are disbursed. The
disbursement agreement will identify the Recipient and include any provisions
that HDFC determines necessary to fulfill the program’s requirements and
objectives. These provisions may include, but are not limited to: general
conditions for disbursement; conditions that must be satisfied before individual
disbursements; procedures for submitting draw requests; remedies in the event

§ 32115. Defaults & Remedies.
(a) If the Sponsor breaches any provision of the loan document, promissory note, deed
of trust, or any other Project agreement, HDFC may issue written notice to of the
breach and the opportunity to cure. The Sponsor shall have at least 30 days from
the date of such notice to cure. If the breach is not cured to HDFC’s satisfaction
within that time, HDFC may declare a default and pursue legal remedies, including
the following:
(1) HDFC may accelerate all amounts due under the loan, including principal and
interest, and demand immediate repayment, as well as repayment of any grant
award. If these accelerated amounts are not fully repaid, HDFC may initiate
foreclosure in accordance with the deed of trust or grant security agreement and
applicable state law.
(2) HDFC may seek court action for specific performance, breach of contract, or for
appointment of a receiver to operate the Affordable Housing Development in
compliance with HDFC requirements.
(3) HDFC may pursue any other remedies available under the agreement or
applicable law.
(4) If the Project has multiple HDFC funding sources, all such funding shall be
cross-defaulted. A default under one source constitutes a default under all other
HDFC funding for the Project.
(b) If the breach involves charging tenants Rent or other fees above amounts allowed
under the Regulatory Agreement, HDFC may require repayment of the excess to the
affected households. In enforcing the Regulatory Agreement, HDFC may also seek
repayment of such overcharges as an additional remedy.
(c) HDFC may cancel loan or grant commitments under any of the following conditions:
(1) The HDFC’s objectives and requirements reflected in program documents
cannot be met;
(2) The Project cannot proceed in a timely manner in accordance with approved
plans and schedules;
(3) Special conditions have not been fulfilled within required time periods; or
(4) There has been a material, unapproved change in the Project or in the Sponsor’s
principals or management.
(d) If the Sponsor demonstrates good cause, HDFC may extend the compliance
deadline and shall provide the extension in writing.
(e) Upon receiving a notice of intent to cancel the loan or grant, the Sponsor may
appeal to HDFC’s Executive Director.
(f) HDFC may use additional funding amounts to cure or prevent a Sponsor’s default
that jeopardizes the Project’s Fiscal Integrity or HDFC’s security, including defaults
in mortgage payments, property taxes, insurance, or required reserves. Any such
advance is at HDFC’s sole discretion, creates no entitlement, and becomes part of
the HDFC loan, or due to HDFC upon demand. HDFC may take any necessary
actions, including foreclosure or forced sale, to prevent future occurrences and
ensure compliance with applicable agreements.
