§ 34000. Definitions.
Accessible Housing Unit – Refers to a “Housing Unit with Mobility Features” and/or
“Housing Units with Hearing/Vision Features” as defined below:
1. A “Housing Unit with Mobility Features” means a housing Unit that is located on
an accessible route and complies with the requirements of 24 CFR § 8.22 and all
applicable provisions of Uniform Federal Accessibility Standards (UFAS) or the
comparable provisions of the Alternative Accessibility Standard, including but not
limited to §§ 809.2 through 809.4 of the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible
Design. A Housing Unit with Mobility Features can be approached, entered, and
used by persons with mobility Disabilities, including individuals who use
wheelchairs. Such Units must also comply with California Building Code §11B.
2. A “Housing Unit with Hearing/Vision Features” means a housing Unit that
complies with 24 CFR § 8.22, and all applicable provisions of UFAS or the
comparable provisions of the Alternative Accessibility Standard, including but not
limited to § 809.5 of the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design. Such Units
must also comply with California Building Code § 11B.
Acquisition – Acquiring improved or unimproved real property and in compliance with 24
Adaptive Reuse – The retrofitting and repurposing of an existing building to create new
residential rental units. Adaptive Reuse does not include rehabilitation of an existing
residential rental building or other construction affecting existing residential rental
housing units, as defined by the U.S. Census Bureau. Adaptive Reuse may include the
conversion of an existing hotel, motel, or other nonresidential building to residential
rental housing, provided the hotel or motel is not occupied as a place of residence at the
time of application.
Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing – Taking meaningful actions, in addition to
combating discrimination, that overcome patterns of segregation, address disparities in
housing needs and access to opportunity, replace segregated living patterns with
integrated and balanced living patterns, transform racially and ethnically concentrated
areas of poverty into areas of opportunity, and foster inclusive communities free from
barriers that restrict access to opportunity based on protected characteristics.
Affordable Housing Development – Affordable Housing Development – A structure or
set of structures with common financing, ownership, and management, and which
collectively contains 5 or more Units (except HOME Projects which may contain fewer
than 5 Units, and Projects proposed by Tribal Entities which may contain 4 units), that
are or will be subject to HDFC-approved affordability, occupancy, and/or rent
restrictions as a condition of HDFC funding offered as rental housing. Such dwelling
Units may include Single Room Occupancy Units as defined in Health & Saf. Code, §
50675.2(d). No more than one of the dwelling Units may be occupied as a primary
residence by a person or household who is the owner of the structure or structures;
except as may be permitted as outlined in Chapter 3, Program-Specific Supplements.
“Affordable Housing Development” does not include any “health facility” as defined by
Health & Saf. Code, § 1250 or any “alcoholism or drug abuse recovery or treatment
facility” as defined by Health & Saf. Code, § 11834.02. An Affordable Housing
Development includes, without limitation, the real property, the improvements located
thereon, and all fixtures and appurtenances related thereto. Note: Where any Applicant
is demonstrating experience in its application for Program funding, the term “Affordable
Housing Development” will also be interpreted to mean a structure or set of structures
with common financing, ownership, and management, and which collectively include(s)
five or more dwelling Units (except HOME Projects which may contain fewer than 5
Units and Projects proposed by Tribal Entities which may contain 4 units) that are
subject to the affordability, occupancy, and/or rent restrictions of any Local Public Entity,
any Tribal Entity, CTCAC/CDLAC, or the federal government. In such cases, the term is
also subject to any additional requirements that appear in context.
Affordable Rent(s) – Rents established in the annual Multifamily Tax Subsidy Projects
(MTSP) Regular Income and Rent Limits published by HUD annually for each county to
determine rent limits.
Agricultural Land(s) – The following categories of farmland in the California Department
of Conservation’s Farmland Mapping and Monitoring Program (FMMP) tool (California
Important Farmland Finder): Prime Farmland, Farmland of Statewide Importance,
Unique Farmland, Farmland of Local Importance, and Grazing Land.
Annual Operating Budget – The Project-level budget prepared for each Fiscal Year
showing projected Operating Income, Operating Expenses, Debt Service, reserve
deposits, Replacement Reserve activity, Supportive Services expenses where
applicable, and resulting cash flow for the Housing Development.
Appraisal – A professional assessment that determines the estimated market value of a
piece of property. Appraisals shall meet the requirements specified in Section 32065
Appraisal Requirements.
Area Median Income – The most recent applicable county median family income
published by California Tax Credit Allocation Committee (CTCAC). For Tribal Entity
Sponsors, if the HUD income for a county/parish located within a Tribal Entity’s service
area is lower than the United States median, the Tribal Entity may use the United States
median income limit.
Assisted Unit – “Assisted Unit” is a term not used within the HDFC Regulations. See:
Restricted Unit.
At Risk of Homelessness – An individual or family that does not currently meet the
definition of “Homeless” but lacks sufficient resources or support networks to prevent
Homelessness and meets the applicable federal or program-specific criteria for being at
risk of Homelessness, including income, housing instability, pending loss of housing, or
other qualifying conditions recognized by the applicable funding source.
At-Risk Project – A Project or property that is “at risk of conversion” and loss of
affordable housing Units, as defined by Rev. & Tax. Code, § 17058(c)(4) and by 4 CCR
Award – A funding commitment made by HDFC to a Sponsor to expend toward eligible
uses.
Award Commitment Letter – The one or more agreements with the Sponsor that is more
fully described in Section 32083 and Section 32110.
BIA – The Bureau of Indian Affairs.
Capital Improvement Project – The construction, rehabilitation, demolition, relocation,
preservation, acquisition, or other physical improvement of a capital asset, as defined in
Gov. Code, § 16727(a), that is an integral part of, or necessary to facilitate the
development of, a Qualifying Infill Project.
Capitalized Operating Subsidy Reserve (COSR) – Funds as described in Section 33000
of these Regulations.
Case Manager – A social worker or other qualified person who assists in individualized
service planning, and the assessment, coordination, monitoring, referral, and advocacy
of services to meet tenants’ Supportive Services’ needs, including, but not limited to,
access to medical and mental health services, substance abuse services, vocational
training, employment, home and community-based services and crisis management and
interventions. Resident service coordinators are not Case Managers. In certain high
needs populations, may be Comprehensive Case Management and include
individualized services planning and the provision of connections to mental health,
substance abuse, employment, health, housing retention, and similar services.
CCR –California Code of Regulations.
Certificate of Completion – A written certification, notice, or other official document
issued by an authorized public agency, lender, investor, architect, engineer, or other
approved party confirming that construction, rehabilitation, conversion, or another
approved scope of work has been completed in accordance with applicable
requirements and the Project is ready for occupancy.
CFR – Code of Federal Regulations.
Chronic Homelessness – An individual or family that meets the federal definition of
“chronic homelessness,” including an individual with a Disability who has been
continuously Homeless for at least 12 months, has experienced at least 4 episodes of
Homelessness totaling at least 12 months over a three-year period, or a family with an
adult head of household who meets those criteria.
Co-Sponsor – The non-profit, for-profit corporation, limited liability company and/or
limited partnership that applies jointly with an eligible Sponsor for an Award of HDFC
funds, but that does not necessarily independently meet the eligibility requirements to
be a Sponsor.
1. Co-Sponsors collaborate on the same Project but don’t necessarily form a new
business entity.
2. Co-Sponsor roles may be unequal, with one taking on more responsibility than
the other.
Commercial Space – Any nonresidential space located in or on the property of a Project
that is, or is proposed to be, used to serve clients or customers not exclusive to
residents of the Project.
Community-Based Developer – A type of proposed Sponsor that meets the
requirements described in Section 32020.
Community Benefit Programs – Such programs include, but are not limited to, the
following:
1. Free or reduced-cost childcare, after-school care, youth development, or adult
daycare programs.
2. Community center facilities that are staffed and open to the public at least once a
week or a minimum of 7 hours each week.
3. A medical clinic with a physician, physician’s assistant, or nurse practitioner
onsite for a minimum of 40 hours each week.
4. Technical assistance or lending to, or investment in, at least 10 small businesses
within 5 miles of the proposed Project.
5. Job training, digital literacy training, college outreach (linking potential students to
college resources and information), or other employment or educational
programs or outreach.
6. Financial counseling, housing counseling, free tax return assistance, or other
economic empowerment programs.
7. Food distribution programs.
Community Housing Development Organization (CHDO) – A private nonprofit,
community-based service organization that meets the applicable federal HOME
program requirements for a community Housing Development organization and is
eligible to own, develop, or sponsor affordable housing activities where authorized by
program requirements.
Community Revitalization Area – An area for which a comprehensive Community
Revitalization Plan has been adopted and efforts specific to that plan have occurred
which satisfies all of the following requirements at the time of application, as reasonably
determined by HDFC:
1. A Federal Opportunity Zone, Choice Neighborhood, or HUD-approved
Neighborhood Revitalization Strategy Area;
2. A Disadvantaged Community as defined in this section;
3. Any Qualified Census Tract or equivalent geographic area defined by the Census
Bureau in which at least 50% of the households have an income of less than
60% AMI;
4. A racially/ethnically concentrated area of poverty (R/ECAP);
5. A census tract or block group designated as “high poverty and segregated” in the
most recently updated TCAC/HCD Opportunity Area Map; or
6. A Neighborhood Change area as designated in the most recently updated
TCAC/HCD Opportunity Area and Neighborhood Change Map.
A Community Revitalization Area must include a specific geographic area and
explicitly cannot be jurisdiction-wide.
Community Revitalization Plan – A plan for concerted community revitalization efforts
which satisfies all of the following requirements at the time of application, as reasonably
determined by HDFC:
1. The Plan has committed funding through public and/or private investments as
demonstrated by an adopted neighborhood or site-specific plan that explicitly
calls for the provision of deed-restricted affordable housing Units;
2. The Plan must have been adopted or updated by the jurisdiction within the last 8
years;
3. The Plan must be sufficient in size and scope to have a significant and lasting
impact on the community;
4. The plan must not be initiated by the Project Applicant or Sponsor, with the
exception of a Public Housing Authority; and
5. The letter must also explain how the Project will contribute to the community's
planned revitalization and include, but is not limited to, a description of the
following community engagement, investment, and other revitalization efforts:
a. Enhancement of community amenities and services in the area, including,
but not limited to, workforce development, open space, parks, recreation
centers, educational facilities, transportation and mobility, storm water
systems, sewer systems, and utility infrastructure.
b. Measurable and significant local government funds, not including funds for
the Project, that have been expended in the past 5 years or are being
expended in the next 5 years to improve the community amenities and
services as illustrated in subsection (a) of this section.
c. Projects, not including the proposed Project, that have been completed
within the past 5 years or are underway or committed to be completed that
contribute to community revitalization, including, but not limited to, retail,
office, and housing projects.
Comprehensive Case Management – Individualized services planning and the provision
of connections to mental health, substance abuse, employment, health, housing
retention, and similar services.
Coordinated Entry System (CES) – A centralized or coordinated process developed
pursuant to 24 CFR § 578.7(a)(8), as that section read on May 1, 2016, designed to
coordinate program participant intake, assessment, and provision of referrals. A
Coordinated Entry System covers the geographic area, is easily accessed by individuals
and families seeking housing or services, is well advertised, and includes a
comprehensive and standardized assessment tool.
Culturally Competent Services – Services that respect diversity in the community and
that respond effectively across cultures, regardless of differences in language,
communication styles, abilities, disabilities, beliefs, attitudes, and behaviors.
Debt Service – The scheduled payment of principal, interest, mortgage insurance
premiums, credit enhancement costs, bond-related payments, or other required
payments due on Project debt or financing obligations during a stated period.
Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) – The ratio of a Project’s net Operating Income or
other approved cash flow measure to required Debt Service for the same period, used
to evaluate whether Project income is sufficient to support required debt payments.
Developer – A private for-profit or nonprofit organization or Tribal Entity that owns or
has site control over real property and arranges for design, financing, professional,
technical, and construction services in connection with a housing project to develop
affordable housing. A nonprofit organization formed as a special purpose entity by a
non-federally recognized tribe may be considered a Developer, if the tribe meets all
other Developer eligibility requirements. See also: Sponsor.
Developer Fee – All funds paid at any time as compensation for developing the
proposed Project, to include all processing agent fees, Developer overhead and profit,
construction management oversight fees if provided by the Developer, personal
guarantee fees, syndicator consulting fees, and reserves in excess of those customarily
required by multi-family housing lenders.
Disability or Persons with Disabilities – A person who has a physical, mental, or
developmental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities, a
record of such impairment, or being regarded as having such an impairment, as defined
by applicable federal and state law. For HDFC programs, the term includes “disability”
definitions applicable under the ADA, FEHA, HUD regulations, and any program-
specific requirements.
Disadvantaged Community (DAC) – Defined by the following conditions:
1. Census tracts with the highest 25% of CalEnviroScreen 5.0 overall scores.
2. Census tracts with the highest 5% of CalEnviroScreen 5.0 pollution burden
scores.
3. Census tracts that have at least 25% overlap with a 2022 DAC census tract
based on CalEnviroScreen 4.0.
4. Lands under the control of federally recognized Tribes, with updated Tribal
boundaries data.
For purposes of this designation, a Tribe may establish that a particular area of land
is under its control even if not represented as such on CalEPA’s DAC map and
therefore should be considered a DAC by requesting a consultation with the CalEPA
Deputy Secretary for Environmental Justice, Tribal Affairs and Border Relations at
TribalAffairs@calepa.ca.gov.
Eligible Basis – The total depreciable basis of residential and eligible Project
improvements used to calculate tax credit eligibility and basis limitations.
Eligible Household – A household whose income does not exceed the regulatory limits
of the applicable HDFC funding sources, as calculated in accordance with the
regulations and procedures governing the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit program, as
administered by CTCAC, or other income limits agreed to by a Project Sponsor and
HDFC. Household income will be calculated based on Units in accordance with CTCAC
rules and procedures.
Emerging Developer – A type of proposed Sponsor that meets the requirements
described in Section 32020.
Enforceable Financing Commitment – Has the same meaning as defined, as may be
subsequently amended, in the CTCAC regulations in 4 CCR § 10325(f)(3).
Established Developer – A type of proposed Sponsor that meets the requirements
described in Section 32020.
Executive Committee – The Housing Development and Finance Executive Committee
established under Health & Saf. Code, § 54940.
Executive Director – The Executive Director of the Housing Development and Finance
Committee.
Extremely Low-Income Families and Households – Households with Gross Incomes not
exceeding 30% of Area Median Income as set forth in Health & Saf. Code, § 50106.
Factory-Built Housing – As set forth in Health & Saf. Code, § 19971, a residential
building, dwelling unit, or an individual dwelling room or combination of rooms thereof,
or building component, assembly, or system manufactured in such a manner that all
concealed parts or processes of manufacture cannot be inspected before installation at
the building site without disassembly, damage, or destruction of the part, including Units
designed for use as part of an institution for resident or patient care, that is either wholly
manufactured or is in substantial part manufactured at an offsite location to be wholly or
partially assembled onsite in accordance with building standards published in the
California Building Standards Code and other regulations adopted by the commission
pursuant to § 19990. Factory-Built Housing does not include a mobile home, as defined
in § 18008, a recreational vehicle, as defined in § 18010.5, or a commercial modular, as
defined in § 18012.5.
Fair Housing Law(s) – Has the same meaning as defined, as may be subsequently
amended, in the CTCAC regulations in 4 CCR § 10302.
Farmworker – An individual engaged in agriculture who derives, or prior to retirement or
Disability derived, a substantial portion of their income from agricultural employment,
where “agriculture” includes farming in all of its branches, and, among other things,
includes the cultivation and tillage of the soil, dairying, the production, cultivation,
growing, and harvesting of any agricultural or horticultural commodities; the raising of
livestock, bees, furbearing animals, or poultry, and any practices (including forestry, and
lumbering operations) performed by a farmer or on a farm as incident to or in
conjunction with such farming operations, including preparation for and delivery to
storage or to market or to carriers for transportation to market (Lab. Code, § 1140.4(a));
work done by any person who works on or off the farm in the processing of any
agricultural commodity until it is shipped for distribution, whether or not such person is
encompassed within the definition specified in Lab. Code, § 1140.4(b). Equivalent to
“Agricultural Employee” as defined in Health & Saf. Code, § 50517.5(e)(1)
Farmworker Household – A Farmworker or Farmworkers and other persons who reside,
or will reside, with a Farmworker in a Restricted Unit.
Farmworker Housing – Housing in which at least 25% of the Units are available to, and
occupied by, farmworkers and their households. HDFC may permit an owner to
temporarily house non-farmworkers in Vacant Units in the event of a disaster or other
critical occurrence. However, such emergency shelter shall only be permitted if there
are no pending qualified farmworker household applications for residency.
Fiscal Integrity – That the total Operating Income plus funds released pursuant to the
HDFC loan documents from the Operating Reserve account is sufficient to:
1. pay all current Operating Expenses;
2. pay all current Debt Service (excluding deferred interest);
3. fully fund all reserve accounts (other than the Operating Reserve account)
established pursuant to the HDFC loan documents; and
4. pay other extraordinary costs permitted by the HDFC loan documents. The ability
to pay any or all of the permitted annual distributions shall not be considered in
determining Fiscal Integrity.
Fiscal Year – The 12-month accounting period used by HDFC, the Sponsor, the Project
owner, or the Housing Development for financial reporting, budgeting, audited financial
statements, operating statements, and compliance reporting, as applicable.
Floor Area Ratio (FAR) – The square footage of the floor area of a building divided by
the site square footage, excluding therefrom dedicated streets, sidewalks, parks, and
open space. The floor area of a building is the sum of the gross area of each floor of the
building, excluding mechanical space, cellar space, floor space in open balconies,
enclosed parking and elevators or stair bulkheads. Multiplying the FAR by the area of
the site produces the minimum amount of floor area required in a building on the lot. For
example, on a 10,000 square-foot site in a district with a minimum FAR of 1.5, the floor
area of a building must be at least 15,000 square feet.
Gross Income – Total income from all sources anticipated to be received by a
household before deductions, exclusions, or adjustments, determined in accordance
with 25 CCR § 6914 and any applicable federal or program-specific income
determination requirements.
HDFC Pool – The pool of state bonds as described in Section 31005.
HDFC Request – Requests for HDFC-awarded funding, including all federal and state
loans and grants, as well as state tax credits available pursuant to Section 31005(e).
High-Density Housing – A Housing Type that meets the requirements described in
Section 32040(b)(1)(G).
High-Rise Project – A Project with the same meaning as defined, as may be
subsequently amended, in the CTCAC regulations in 4 CCR § 10302(jj).
High Segregation and Poverty Area – As specified on the CTCAC/HCD Opportunity
Area Map.
Homeless or Homelessness – An individual or family that lacks a fixed, regular, and
adequate nighttime residence, is living in a shelter or place not meant for human
habitation, is imminently losing housing, is fleeing domestic violence or other dangerous
conditions, or otherwise meets the applicable federal or program-specific definition of
“homeless” or “homelessness.” Homeless and Homelessness also may be defined
within Health and Saf. Code, § 50675.15 for Medi-Cal services or as defined by
Veterans Set-Aside funds.
Homeownership Affordable Housing Development or Homeownership AHD – New
construction, Adaptive Reuse, or substantial rehabilitation of housing Units which shall
initially be sold to and occupied by qualified households and shall be subject to a resale
restriction for at least 30 years.
Housing and Accessibility Requirements – Has the same meaning as defined, as may
be subsequently amended, in the CTCAC regulations in 4 CCR § 10302.
Housing Development – For the purpose of housing funded by HDFC, any work or
undertaking of new construction or Rehabilitation, or the Acquisition of existing
residential structures in good condition, for the provision of housing that is financed
pursuant to the provisions of this division for the primary purpose of providing decent,
safe, and sanitary housing for persons and families of Lower Income, or, for MIP
program, Moderate Incomes. “Housing Development” also means housing financed
pursuant to this part for rental occupancy of, for resale to, or sold to, persons and
families of Low or Moderate Income. Notwithstanding other provisions of this section,
“Housing Development” does not include a work or undertaking financed by a
neighborhood improvement loan. A Housing Development may include housing for
other economic groups as part of an overall plan to develop new or rehabilitated
communities or neighborhoods, where housing for persons and families of Low or
Moderate Income is a primary goal. A Housing Development may include any buildings,
land, equipment, facilities, or other real or personal property that the agency determines
pursuant to its rules and regulations to be necessary or convenient in connection with
the provision of housing pursuant to this division, including, but not limited to, streets,
sewers, utilities, parks, site preparation, landscaping, and other nonhousing facilities,
such as administrative, community, health, recreational, educational, commercial
facilities, and child-care facilities that the agency determines are an integral part of a
Housing Development or developments.
“Housing Development” includes the Acquisition of a residential structure by a nonprofit
housing Sponsor, whether or not including Rehabilitation, for the purpose of forming a
limited-equity housing cooperative as defined in Civ. Code, § 817.
Housing Development and Finance Committee (HDFC) – Unless the context clearly
requires otherwise, references in these Regulations to “HDFC” include the Committee
staff, the Executive Committee, the Executive Director, and any other State Department
or Agency or authorized entity performing responsibilities on behalf of HDFC pursuant
to applicable law, these Regulations, or an interagency agreement approved by HDFC.
Nothing in this definition shall be construed to alter or diminish the independent
statutory authority of any participating agency.
Housing Type – A category of housing as defined in Section 32040, Housing Types, of
these Regulations.
Incorporated City – A municipal jurisdiction that has been formally established under the
laws of the State of California and operates with its own local government, including an
elected governing body, charter or municipal code, and administrative authority. An
Incorporated City exercises land use authority within its boundaries, including zoning,
permitting, and regulatory oversight applicable to residential development, and is
recognized by the state as a legally constituted local government entity.
In-Lieu Fees – Fees paid to a public agency or other authorized entity in satisfaction of
an affordable housing, inclusionary housing, impact mitigation, replacement housing, or
other local housing obligation, when payment of the fee is authorized by applicable law,
ordinance, agreement, or program requirement.
IRC – Internal Revenue Code.
Joint Venture – A formal business arrangement where two (2) or more parties create a
partnership, often forming a new legal entity, to pursue a specific project or business
goal.
1. Each party contributes resources (money, staff, assets, expertise).
2. Risks, profits, and control are shared according to written agreement.
Land Basis – The portion of project cost or basis attributable to the Acquisition,
contribution, value, or carrying cost of land and other non-depreciable real property
interests, as distinguished from depreciable building basis or improvement costs.
Large City Downtown – An area designated as a downtown, central business district, or
core area in local planning documents in one of the following cities: Anaheim,
Bakersfield, Fresno, Irvine, Long Beach, Los Angeles, Oakland, Riverside, Sacramento,
San Diego, San Francisco, San Jose, Santa Ana, and Stockton. These California cities
have a population exceeding 300,000 according to California Department of Finance
data.
Large Family Housing – A Housing Type that meets the requirements described in
Section 32040(b)(1)(A).
Lead Service Provider (LSP) – The organization that has overall responsibility for the
provisions of Supportive Services and implementation of the Supportive Services plan in
the Project. The LSP may directly provide Case Management services, as applicable, or
contract with other agencies that provide services. For HUD-VASH tenants, the LSP will
enable the applicable Veterans Affairs Case Manager to administer services in
accordance with the HUD-VA Supportive Housing (VASH) Program.
LIHTC – Low-income housing tax credits.
Local Inclusionary Programs – Local laws, ordinances, policies, agreements, or
programs that require or incentivize the production, preservation, dedication, funding, or
restriction of affordable housing Units as part of residential or Mixed-Use Development.
Local Public Entity – A city, county, city and county, housing authority, redevelopment
successor or housing successor agency, joint powers authority, tribal or local
governmental body, or other public entity authorized under state or federal law to own,
sponsor, develop, finance, or administer affordable housing or related public purposes.
Low(er)-Income Families and Households – Households with Gross Incomes not
exceeding 80% of Area Median Income as set forth in Health & Saf. Code, § 50079.5.
Low Resource Area – As specified on the CTCAC/HCD Opportunity Area Map.
LTRO – The Land, Titles, and Records Office of the BIA.
Major Transit Stop – Has the same meaning as defined in Pub. Resources Code, §
21064.3, as may be subsequently amended: A site containing any of the following:
1. An existing rail or bus rapid transit station.
2. A ferry terminal served by either a bus or rail transit service.
3. The intersection of two or more major bus routes with a frequency of service
interval of 20 minutes or less during the morning and afternoon peak commute
periods.
Market Rate – Housing, Units, rents, sales prices, or project components that are not
subject to income, rent, affordability, occupancy, resale, or other affordability restrictions
imposed by HDFC, another public agency, a regulatory agreement, a recorded
covenant, or applicable program requirements.
Migrant Farmworker – A Farmworker who is required to be absent from a permanent
place of residence for the purpose of seeking or performing seasonal agricultural
employment, including household members where permitted by applicable program
requirements.
Mixed-Use Development – A development consisting of residential Units and
compatible nonresidential uses.
Mobility Features – Located on an accessible route and compliant with 24 CFR. part
8.22, California Building Code Ch. 11B, Division 4 and §§ 809.2 through 809.4, and all
applicable provisions of Uniform Federal Accessibility Standards or comparable
provisions of the Alternative Accessibility Standard, including but not limited to §§ 809.2
through 809.4 of the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design. A housing Unit with
Mobility Features can be approached, entered, and used by persons with mobility
disabilities, including individuals who use wheelchairs.
Moderate-Income Families and Households – Households whose Gross Incomes do not
exceed the moderate-income limits applicable to the project or program, generally 120%
of Area Median Income adjusted for household size, as published or accepted by HCD,
HUD, CalHFA, or the applicable funding source.
Moderate Resource Area – As specified on the CTCAC/HCD Opportunity Area Map.
Multifamily Pipeline Projects – Projects that have received financing from designated
state multifamily programs prior to January 1, 2027, and are fully funded aside from tax
credits and bonds, the bond issuer may apply directly to CDLAC or CTCAC for an
allocation of the 2027 HDFC Pool with a letter of support from HDFC. This pathway is
available until November 1, 2027.
Native American Housing and Self Determination Act (NAHASDA) – Native American
Housing Assistance and Self-Determination Act of 1996, Pub. L. 103-330, 25 USC
4101, et seq., as amended.
Net Cash Flow – The cash remaining from project operations after payment of approved
Operating Expenses, required Debt Service, developer fee, required reserve deposits,
approved asset management fees, and other required payments, as calculated under
applicable loan documents, regulatory agreements, partnership agreements, or program
requirements – as described in Section 32063(d)(2).
Net Density – The total number of housing Units per acre of land to be developed for
residential or mixed use, excluding allowed deductible areas. Allowed deductible areas
are public dedications of land which are for public streets, public sidewalks, public Open
Space, and public drainage facilities. Non-allowed deductible areas include utility
easements, setbacks, private drives and walkways, general landscaping, common
areas and facilities, off street parking, and traditional drainage facilities exclusive to a
development project. Mitigations required for development will not be included in the
allowed deductible areas.
Non-Entitlement – A California city or county that does not receive HOME funding
directly from HUD, is not designated by HUD as a Participating Jurisdiction (PJ), not
part of a HUD recognized HOME consortium, and not covered by an urban county
agreement that gets HOME funds directly. Each year, HCD will publish the current list of
Non-Entitlement areas based on HUD’s official PJ and consortium designations and
State records of urban county agreements. That published list becomes the rule for that
program year.
Operating Expenses – The amount approved by HDFC that is necessary to pay for the
recurring expenses of the Project, such as utilities, maintenance, management, taxes,
licenses, and Supportive Services Costs, but not including Debt Service or required
reserve account deposits.
Operating Income – All income generated in connection with operation of the Project
including rental income for Restricted Units, rental income for laundry and equipment
rental fees, rental subsidy payments, and interest on any accounts, other than approved
reserve accounts, related to the Affordable Housing Development. "Operating Income"
does not include Commercial Space or commercial use, security and equipment
deposits, payments to the Sponsor for Supportive Services not included in HDFC-
approved operating budget, cash contributed by the Sponsor, or tax benefits received
by the Sponsor.
Operating Reserve – Funds capitalized at or before loan closing, conversion, or another
approved project milestone and held to support project operations, operating deficits,
lease-up risk, service obligations, or other approved operating needs in accordance with
applicable loan documents, regulatory agreements, partnership agreements, or program
requirements.
Opportunity Area Map – A map or series of maps approved annually by CTCAC/HCD
as the CTCAC/HCD Opportunity Area Map.
Permanent Loan Closing – The point at which a Project transitions from construction
financing to permanent financing, usually after construction is completed, cost
certification is accepted, and occupancy thresholds are met.
Preservation – A Project that meets any of the criteria of Section 32040 of these
Regulations and is a Rehabilitation Project.
Pre-Subdivision Parcel – A parcel of real property as it existed before subdivision, lot
line adjustment, parcel map, final map, condominium map, or other division of land,
when that preexisting parcel is relevant to eligibility, site control, density, affordability,
infrastructure, or program requirements.
Private Activity Bonds – Tax-exempt bonds or other qualified private activity bonds
issued under federal and state law to finance eligible private or nonprofit activities,
including qualified residential rental projects, subject to applicable volume cap,
allocation, tax, bond, and program requirements.
Project – The real property and all improvements thereon, of an Affordable Housing
Development that has applied for, been awarded, or received HDFC funding.
Property Manager – The person or entity responsible for day-to-day management,
leasing, rent collection, occupancy compliance, tenant relations, maintenance
coordination, reporting, and other property operations for a Housing Development,
whether acting directly or through an approved management agent.
Qualified Residential Rental Bonds (QRRP Bonds) – A qualified private activity bond
issued to finance Qualified Residential Rental Projects pursuant to an allocation from
the QRRP Pool, as defined in 4 CCR § 5000.
Qualified Residential Rental Project (QRRP) – A residential rental project that satisfies
the applicable federal tax requirements for qualified residential rental projects financed
with tax-exempt Private Activity Bonds, including applicable income, rent, occupancy,
use, and compliance requirements.
Qualifying Infill Project – A residential or mixed-use residential Project located within an
urbanized area on a site that has been previously developed, or on a vacant site where
at least 75% of the perimeter of the site adjoins parcels that are developed with Urban
Uses.
Recipient – The eligible Sponsor, or an affiliate of the Sponsor (e.g. a special purpose
entity) that is directly or indirectly controlled by the Sponsor and is designated to receive
the disbursement of funds awarded to the Sponsor by HDFC. Controlled means that the
Sponsor has the power to direct management operations of the affiliate entity, whether
through ownership or through rights in the governing documents. Control may be
exercised directly, through intermediate controlled entities, or through control of the
managing general partner of a limited partnership Recipient.
Region – The territory of the metropolitan planning organization within which a Project is
located, or the territory of the regional transportation planning agency within which a
Project is located if the site is located outside of the boundaries of a metropolitan
planning organization.
Rehabilitation – The term defined in accordance with Health & Saf. Code, § 50096,
including improvements and repairs made to a substandard residential structure
acquired for the purpose of preserving its affordability.
Replacement Reserve – Funds capitalized at or before loan closing, conversion, or
another approved project milestone and held for future repair, replacement,
rehabilitation, or capital needs of the Housing Development in accordance with
applicable loan documents, regulatory agreements, partnership agreements, or program
requirements.
Restricted Unit – A Unit that is subject to rent and/or occupancy restrictions as a result
of financial assistance provided under any HDFC funding awards or as imposed by
CTCAC or any other public agency.
Restructure – A modification, workout, refinancing, recapitalization, amendment,
extension, assumption, transfer, or other change to existing project financing,
ownership, regulatory obligations, repayment terms, or operating requirements intended
to preserve affordability, address project distress, or support long-term project viability.
Re-syndication – The recapitalization of an Affordable Housing Development through a
new allocation or investment of low-income housing tax credits, typically involving new
ownership, investor, financing, Rehabilitation, or regulatory commitments while
preserving or extending affordability restrictions.
Rural (Area) – Has the meaning set forth in Health & Saf. Code, § 50199.21. This
definition may be changed by HDFC to conform to changes in federal programs or
updates in methodology by CTCAC.
SAM.gov Exclusions (formerly known as the Excluded Parties List System, or EPLS) –
A publicly accessible database of individuals and entities barred from receiving federal
contracts, grants, loans, or other financial assistance.
Scattered Site – A Project site in which the parcels of land are not contiguous except for
the interposition of a road, street, stream or similar interposition. For Acquisition and/or
Rehabilitation Projects with one pre-existing project-based Section 8 contract in effect
for all the sites, there shall be no limit on the number or proximity of sites. For
Acquisition and/or Rehabilitation Projects with any of the following: (A) existing federal
or state rental assistance or operating subsidies, (B) an existing CTCAC regulatory
agreement, or (C) an existing regulatory agreement with a federal, state, or local public
entity, the number of sites shall be limited to five, unless the Executive Director
approves a higher number, and all sites shall be either within the boundaries of the
same city, within a 10-mile diameter circle in the same county, or within the same
county if no location is within a city having a population of five-hundred thousand
(500,000) or more. For new construction projects and all other Acquisition and/or
Rehabilitation Projects, the number of sites shall be limited to five, and all sites shall be
within a 1-mile diameter circle within the same county.
Schedule of Rental Income – A Project-level schedule identifying each unit or unit type,
rent limits, actual rents, utility allowances, tenant-paid rent, rental assistance, income
restrictions, occupancy restrictions, Vacancies, and other rental income information,
excluding income from tenant-based vouchers, required for underwriting, compliance,
asset management, or monitoring.
Senior Housing – A Housing Type meeting the requirements of Section 32040(b)(1)(B)
intended for occupancy by older adults or senior households and operated in
accordance with applicable fair housing, civil rights, accessibility, age-restriction,
affordability, and program requirements.
Single Room Occupancy (SRO) Housing or Unit/Studio – Has the same meaning as 4
CCR § 10302. SRO and Studio may be used interchangeably but HDFC recognizes
some jurisdictions may not, and the project shall comply with all local regulations.
Small Jurisdiction – A county with a population of less than 250,000 as of January 1,
2019, or any city within that county.
Special Needs Housing – A Housing Type meeting the requirements of Section 32040
Special Needs Population – Consistent with adopted CTCAC regulations, 4 CCR §
10302. One or more of the following groups who need Supportive Services to maintain
and stabilize their housing:
1. People with Disabilities;
2. At Risk of Homelessness;
3. Individuals with substance use disorders;
4. Frequent users of public health or mental health services, as identified by a public
health or mental health agency;
5. Individuals who are fleeing domestic violence, sexual assault, and human
trafficking;
6. Individuals who are experiencing Homelessness or Chronic Homelessness;
7. Homeless youth as defined in Gov. Code, § 12957(e)(2);
8. Families meeting the definition of “Eligible family” under the Bringing Families
Home program at Welf. & Inst. Code § 16523, who may or may not be
participating in the program.
9. Individuals exiting institutional settings or at risk of placement in an institutional
setting;
10. Older Adults in Need of Supportive Services; or
11. Other specific groups with unique housing needs as determined by the Executive
Director.
Sponsor – The entity that meets the requirements of § 32020 Eligible Applicant of these
Regulations.
Stabilized Occupancy – The point at which a newly constructed or rehabilitated property
achieves consistent, sustainable occupancy levels that meet program or lender
requirements for permanent loan conversion, such as occupancy percentage reached
and occupancy level maintained for a specified period.
Supportive Housing – A Housing Type meeting the requirements of Section
32040(b)(1)(E) with no limit on length of stay, that is occupied by the Supportive
Housing Population and is linked to onsite or offsite services that assist the Supportive
Housing resident that needs support in retaining the housing, improving his or her
health status, and maximizing his or her ability to live and, when possible, work in the
community.
Supportive Housing Population – Persons, including persons with Disabilities, and
families who are “homeless,” as that term is defined by 42 USC § 11302, or who are
“homeless youth,” as that term is defined by Gov. Code, § 12957(e)(2), or who are
exiting institutional settings as defined by Health & Saf. Code, § 50675.14(c)(3).
Veterans also qualify under this definition provided they meet all conditions pursuant to
Health & Saf. Code, § 50675.14(j). Individuals and families currently residing in
Supportive Housing qualify under this definition if the individual or family was
“homeless,” as that term is defined by 42 USC § 11302, when approved for tenancy in
the Supportive Housing Project in which they currently reside.
Supportive Services – Voluntary services, resources, programs, or activities designed to
assist individuals and households in obtaining, maintaining, and succeeding in stable
housing while improving health, safety, economic security, independence, and overall
quality of life. Supportive Services may include, but are not limited to, case
management, housing navigation, tenancy sustaining services, healthcare coordination,
mental health services, substance use disorder services, benefits advocacy,
employment services, educational services, financial capability services, transportation
assistance, childcare assistance, life-skills training, peer support, legal services, and
other services tailored to the needs of the Target Population or Special Needs
Population. Supportive Services may be provided directly, through referral, or through
formal partnerships with qualified service providers and shall be delivered in a manner
consistent with applicable federal, state, and local program requirements.
Supportive Services Reserve – Funds pursuant to Section 32062 available to address
Project supportive service budget deficits attributable to shortfalls in service funding
sources.
Tribal Admissions and Occupancy Standards (TAOS) – Those standards duly adopted
by the federally recognized Indian tribe by resolution or ordinance in accordance with
NAHASDA and Tribal law.
Tribal Entity – A Native American tribe that meets any of the following criteria:
1. Meets the definition of Indian Tribe under 25 USC § 4103(13)(B);
2. Meets the definition of Tribally Designated Housing Entity under 25 USC §
3. Is either:
a. Listed in the Bureau of Indian Affairs Office of Federal Acknowledgement
petitioner list pursuant to Title 25 CFR Part 83 et seq.; or,
b. An Indian Tribe located in California that is on the contact list maintained
by the California Native American Heritage Commission for the purposes
of consultation pursuant to Gov. Code, § 65352.3; and,
c. Has organized a separate legal entity, either a non-profit or for-profit
entity, in compliance with 25 CCR Section 8301(s) and it has
demonstrated to the satisfaction of the Department that the separate legal
entity is controlled by the Tribal Entity Sponsor.
Tribal Housing – A Housing Type that meets the requirements described in Section
Tribal Land – Also referred to as “Indian Country” or “Native American Land,” (1) all land
within the limits of any Indian reservation under the jurisdiction of the United States
Government, notwithstanding the issuance of any patent, and, including rights-of-way
running through the reservation, (2) all dependent Indian communities within the
borders of the United States whether within the original or subsequently acquired
territory thereof, and whether within or without the limits of a state, (3) all Indian
allotments, the Indian titles to which have not been extinguished, including rights-of-way
running through the same as provided at 18 USC § 1151, (4) all lands within the limits of
a Rancheria under the jurisdiction of the United States Government, (5) lands held in
trust by the United States for an Indian Tribe or individual, (6) land held by an Indian
Tribe or individual subject to a restriction by the United States against alienation, and (7)
any additional lands recognized through federal statute, court decision, administrative
action or otherwise qualifying as Indian Country under federal law, or congressional
designation as Indian Country or as land over which a Tribe may exercise governmental
authority, or jurisdiction.
Tribal Trust Land – Land with title held in trust by the United States for the benefit of an
Indian tribe or individual Indian, or land otherwise subject to federal restrictions against
alienation, and that is governed by applicable federal, tribal, state, and program
requirements.
Tribally Designated Housing Entity (TDHE) – The entity authorized or designated by
one or more Indian tribes to receive, administer, or implement housing assistance on
behalf of the tribe or tribes under NAHASDA or other applicable federal or state housing
programs.
Unit – A residential unit that is used as a primary residence by its occupants, including
efficiency units, residential hotel units, and units used as transitional housing.
Urban Center – An area other than a Large City Downtown which is served by more
than one mode of transit.
Urban Uses – Any residential, commercial, industrial, public institutional, transit or
transportation passenger facility, or retail use, or any combination of those uses as set
forth in Health and Saf. Code, § 53559.1(e).
USC – United States Code
Vacancy or Vacant – A dwelling Unit or other rentable space that is not occupied by an
eligible tenant or resident and is available, unavailable, offline, or otherwise not
producing rental income, as determined for underwriting, operations, compliance, lease-
up, or asset management purposes.
Very Low-Income Families and Households – Households with Gross Incomes not
exceeding 50% of Area Median Income as set forth in Health and Saf. Code, § 50105.
Veteran – Any person who actively served within one 1 or more of the military services
of the United States who was called to and released from active duty or active service,
for a period of not less than 90 consecutive days or was discharged from the service
due to a service-connected disability within that 90 day period. This includes all
Veterans regardless of discharge status.
VMT – Vehicle miles traveled.
WIC – The California Welfare and Institutions Code.

Under 24 CFR § 92.253(a) and 24 CFR § 93.303(a), lease

The lease must not contain any of the below prohibited lease terms
1. Agreement to be sued. Agreement by the tenant to be sued,
to admit guilt, or to a judgment in favor of the owner in a
lawsuit brought in connection with the lease;
2. Treatment of property. Agreement by the tenant that the
owner may take, hold, or sell personal property of household
members without notice to the tenant and a court decision on
the rights of the parties. This prohibition, however, does not
apply to an agreement by the tenant concerning disposition
of personal property remaining in the housing unit after the
tenant has moved out of the unit. The owner may dispose of
this personal property in accordance with State law;
3. Excusing owner from responsibility. Agreement by the
tenant not to hold the owner or the owner's agents legally
responsible for any action or failure to act, whether
intentional or negligent;
4. Waiver of notice. Agreement of the tenant that the owner
may institute a lawsuit without notice to the tenant;
5. Waiver of legal proceedings. Agreement by the tenant that
the owner may evict the tenant or household members
without instituting a civil court proceeding in which the tenant
has the opportunity to present a defense, or before a court
decision on the rights of the parties;
